utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everybody in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution this morning, Alex Demirdjian with Lisa Biersay, our case manager Thomas Laugel, and our legal intern Agnes Bugaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic and Christopher Gosnell. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. If there is nothing else, the witness may be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just a couple of follow-up questions on the topic I was asking you about yesterday and your relations with the Office of the Prosecutor. Did you review or assist in preparing any pre-trial briefs or final trial briefs or appeal briefs during your eight years in your association with the office?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and my role in relation to these documents was limited to reviewing the military aspects to see whether, for example, military regulations were accurately reflected or the names of individuals or the positions they held. So I was not involved in any legal -- formulating of legal arguments, I was formulating -- I was exclusively involved in what I would call factual issues within the field of my professional expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that involved interpreting volumes of documents and reaching conclusions; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, but I prefer to be more specific. Reviewing volumes of military documents in order to draw or reaching military conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say -- I said "interpreting volumes of documents and reaching conclusions." Would that include -- would that be part of what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by "interpreting"?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, what I mean by "interpreting," is assessing the significance of -- and the meaning of documents in order to assess responsibility of individuals in relation to events?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that this is a bit of a narrow interpretation of my role. My role provided, among other things, in explaining the military context, for example, when the word "volunteer unit" would pop up then my task would consist in explaining to the lawyers in the team what was meant by that, not only in relation to SFRY armed forces doctrine but also looking at the specific facts. Of course I would also look into command and control issues. So if you talk about military -- about responsibility, if you mean military responsibility, yes; if you mean criminal responsibility, as I said, I did -- I was not involved in legal issues because that is not what I've been trained nor educated in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What about international humanitarian law, have you been trained and educated in that and did you provide advice on that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, like any member of an armed force, I was trained in that. I mean, we had a lot of law in the second year of military academy, but while working here, even if my general knowledge of these issues that I had acquired in my education at the military academy was for sure useful. And of course I familiarised myself with issues like 7(1) and 7(3). I did not express views in my work or in my reports -- I mean, if you review all the eight or nine reports you will not see references to 7(1) or 7(3) or related issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But your interpretation - and I come back to that word - your interpretation of documents for the purposes of providing assistance to the formulation of pre-trial briefs and final trial briefs was informed by your understanding of what we can broadly call responsibility; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I answered the question because I tried to specify what I've done and in relation to the expressions you used "interpretation" and "responsibility," and now you come back again to your broad question. I mean, I've answered the question. I was here as an intelligence analyst military, which means that I look -- I mean general terms into military issues, whether it's command and control, whether it's context, whether it's structures, organisations, roles of military, that was my task. And that was focused on factual issues, i.e., I look at documents. I may have been asked -- also I was also asked to look at witness statements. I look at those factual issues and then I explain what they mean from a military point of view and that's it. And then whatever legal interpretation that may be derived from that, that was not my task, I was not asked to do so, because there's other people in the Office of the Prosecution who are much better qualified than I to take care of these kind of matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And in assessing command and control structures, organisations, roles of the military, in a given week how often did you speak, exchange an e-mail, pick up the telephone and speak with lawyers in the Office of the Prosecutor during your eight years with the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wasn't requested to keep statistics. I don't want to give the impression that I want to argue, but one of your colleagues once asked me how my salary was established. I think it was in the Vukovar case, whether I was paid --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- whether I was paid in according to the results that were achieved. Of course I had daily contacts with other team members and these team members consisted of lawyers, I mean senior trial attorneys, trial attorneys, junior lawyers, interns, as I had contacts with investigators and criminal analysts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is daily?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How many times daily on average?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, from a physical point of view -- for example, when I take lunch, I'm not going to take lunch in isolation in a corner - I don't know where - in the park, so I may bump into people and I may even talk to these people, but it's not like that -- I think you're trying to suggest that the Office of the Prosecutor was maybe on a daily or whatever frequency I will mention the Office of the Prosecutor and especially the lawyers would use that time to give instructions to me as to what I should write or what I should do -- I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let me stop you there. I'm not suggesting anything. All I'm doing is asking factual questions, and it's neither for me nor you to come to these various interpretations or implications. So perhaps we could just stick to the factual side of it and I think you've answered my question and now I'm going to move to the next question which is: Is the military analysis team of which you were a part, is that organisationally part of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The military analysis team was a part of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And who was signing your e-passes over the course of the eight years that you were employed by the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My -- I mean, the first reporting officers I mentioned earlier, those were the team leaders of the military analysis team, and then the second reporting officer I believe it was in most cases Mr. Bob Reid and I forget now the official job title he had -- but I mean he was a senior investigator and then I think he -- whether he was a chief of investigations or -- I think he was chief of investigations for most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In any event, he's a part of the Office of the Prosecutor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to ask you, when would you say - because you haven't been asked this question and it doesn't say in your report - when would you say that the armed conflict started in Croatia? And by "armed conflict," I mean sustained violence between two opposing and organised forces.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that it's -- I won't say it's impossible to answer. There are lots of answers to that question, but I think these answers are also often based on personal interpretations. I would prefer to look into -- to look at the official documents and then to say okay to start from that. If I'm not mistaken it's addressed in the report end of September 1991. What remains of the SFRY Presidency "establishes the existence of an imminent state of war." There has been some debate about the word -- about the use of the expression "establish," because why would they use "establish," they could just declare the state of imminent threat of war. I also know that for the Croatian side the conflict in their view started much earlier, whereas on the Yugoslav or the JNA side even the memorandum we saw --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to try to guide you to an answer to answering the question --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- because you're actually not answering the question, because if you listen to my question I framed it as a matter of actual conduct of hostilities not as a matter of declarations, legal pronouncements, and so forth. And you've looked at many military documents indicating when engagements occurred, and you've interviewed many witnesses who presumably gave you information about that, and you've reported on that in your report. So what I'm asking you is - and you certainly have knowledge of all these issues - when would you say that there was sustained violence between two opposing and organised forces in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again without wanting to argue, I think you formulate the question now differently because initially you talk about an armed conflict. I understand armed conflict as a legal concept whereby indeed you may be able to, based on the contemporaneous documents, establish when it was officially declared. If you talk about sustained violence between two opposing and organised forces in Croatia, I mean there may be some debate about the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If I may intervene, Mr. Theunens, if I understand Mr. Gosnell correctly - and he would point out to me if I got it wrong - the question is when do you say, and this arises out of all your experience, all of your analysis and what not, but the nub of the question is when do you say. Is that correct? Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much, Judge Hall.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification, Your Honours. I would say that in the course of summer 1991 we see a spreading of hostilities in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So would it be at least safe to say that your opinion is that there was an armed conflict as of the 1st of August, 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And by "armed conflict," I'm referring to the definition I gave earlier?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And on page 17 and 18 of your report - and now we're going to go back, I'm afraid, to some potentially tedious discussions of legislation but I'm afraid it has to be done, Mr. Theunens. And on page 17 and 18 of your report you quote from the SFRY Constitution, which is L9 at Prosecution tab 4 but it's fully set out in your report so we don't need to bring the article up, and at Article 240 I'm interested in the second or in the portion of the provision that reads: "Any citizen who takes part in resisting aggression towards the country is a member of the armed forces of the SFRY." So am I right that this is the legal foundation for about I believe what you said yesterday, namely, that if someone takes up arms in defence of the country they're part of the armed forces of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, that is the general principle that is further specified by the additional legislative and other documents we have discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And isn't it true that a person who does so and who is not a member of the JNA is considered to be a part of the Territorial Defence? That could be a yes or no answer, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, if you allow me, I would say yes, given of course the other provisions in the other articles that define who and how they can join the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let's look at page 21 of your report, and there it says, quoting Article 102 of the Law on All People's Defence, and this is SFRY legislation: "Territorial Defence shall comprise all armed formations that are not incorporated into the Yugoslav People's Army." That's the foundation for your statement that if someone takes up arms in defence of the country they become part of the TO; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but now -- okay, I didn't say it like that, but I mean you can summarise it like that, but I would prefer to go to my own answer because it's a bit more complicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let's go to your own answer in Milosevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I apologise for intervening. I don't mean to interrupt, but the question could be potentially misleading if you don't add at the end of the quote "and the police," not just the "SFRY." I just wanted to bring that to your attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yeah, that's a helpful addition. I thank my colleague for that. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So in the Milosevic case, just to be very precise about the answers that you've given, at page 314081 [sic] this is Defence tab 1, 04850 for the record, you said: "It's also noteworthy that the 1974 Constitution states that the armed forces, the SFRY armed forces, consist of the JNA and TO and that all other armed groups or individuals who want to participate in the defence or the armed struggle will be considered members of the TO." That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please don't read fast because the interpreters must keep up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean I don't have the -- my testimony in front of me but I -- I mean, I would agree with it because I still hold that view now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the Law on All People's Defence is a very long document with many provisions, sometimes difficult to reconcile and perhaps understand. Would you just, first of all, agree with that general observation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably long -- I mean, but whether it -- sometimes difficult to reconcile and perhaps understand, I can say that for the issues I was -- I looked at, structure, command and control, and related matters, I notice consistency between not only the constitution, the All People's Defence law, but also the various doctrinal documents. At this moment I don't recall any issues that were difficult to reconcile, but maybe you can draw my attention to one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, that's a fair answer if you -- if you do believe that it's an entirely coherent structure and we'll work our way through some provisions. And perhaps we could just look at Article 1, and this is L10, Prosecution tab 10. I bring this provision to your attention, sir, because I believe it helps provide a flavour as to military doctrine in the SFRY and -- I mean, this is the very beginning of the law. It says: "This law shall regulate the basic rights and duties of working people and citizens, basic and other organisations of associated labour, local communes, and other self management organisations and communities and socio-political and other social organisations in the defence of independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the social order established by the Constitution of the SFRY." Now, my first question for you is very specific and that is: Do you know what a socio-political and other social organisations, that expression, do you know what that encompasses?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are basic entities -- no, I will rephrase that. These are entities or structures that can play role or play a role in the concept of All People's Defence, where basically the entire population is involved or is used in order to defend the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And for me as a -- perhaps from a different culture, I read these provisions and I'm startled because we see all manner of organisational -- almost informal organisational units being apparently recognised in this law. Now, do I understand correctly that what this law is doing is saying that total national defence can be organised around these informal associations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I wouldn't -- I have no recollection that we are talking about informal organisational units. What I recall is that there was a quite formal organisation; for example, in state-owned factories there were defence structures and they would have exercises and they would mobilise and there would be weapons and so on. But this was all very well organised, at least before the dissolution of the SFRY. The same for the TO, we looked at measures that are taken to increase control of weapons or TO, so I wouldn't share the view that it was informal. I would also highlight that no mention is made of any political parties as one of these -- I'm just trying to find --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I didn't say "political parties" and let's leave political parties out of it, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And maybe I used the wrong word in saying informal. Let's say flexible. I mean, for example, could a student union be considered a socio-political organisation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As long as it is legally recognised, then it could be, but again I would prefer to look at the specific documents. And again, in my interpretation "flexible" has nothing to do whether something is official or nonofficial or formal or informal. A military unit has to be flexible, for example, to be able to handle different situations that may arise not only on the battle-field but also, yeah, losses, different missions, and so on, and military unit will be a very formal structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I do understand that military units are a formal structure but what seems to be recognised here in Article 1 is a very flexible approach to what you said was allowing the entire population to participate in the defence. Do you see that Article 1 is an expression of a -- let's start with a general question. Is Article 1 a means by which the entire population, through organisations at a very low level, can organise and participate in national defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the difference in -- between what my answer is and then you come back to your point, you say it's all informal and maybe spontaneous even if I try to understand the gist of your question. What I tried to explain is that indeed there are different organisations that can play a role, but the prime condition is that these organisations have been recognised, I mean there's a legal basis for their existence and for their activities. And as a result of that legal basis, they will accomplish a defined role in the concept of All People's Defence, whereby obviously there will also be a way of co-ordinating the contribution of these organisations, I mean the social organisations, the TO, the military and so on, so that everybody fulfils his or her role in a co-ordinated manner in the defence of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We'll get to the co-ordination issue in a moment. But the issue here is: What are the basic units of people self organising in order to participate in national defence? And I'm suggesting to you that this is a very flexible notion. You say that these groups need to be legally recognised, but on the other hand you say that it potentially could be a student union, it could be a labour union, it could be -- could it be a chess club?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean maybe there's a misunderstanding about the expression of the word "self-management." Self-management was the -- I wouldn't say economical but maybe the economical doctrine in that exists in the SFRY, whereas in the west we had capitalism and in the former Soviet union and other countries you had communism the way they defined it. But self management - and again this is outside my expertise but while working on the former Yugoslavia I had to study a little bit about it - at the end of the day it was very much regulated and there was central control and there was a central revision and so on or state control and state revision. It's the same with these social entities and organisations of associated labour. These are not spontaneous clubs that -- I mean, like a -- I don't know, they didn't have Facebook then, but that spontaneously develop and people come together and say hey we're going to defend the country. It was all regulated for obvious reasons. You cannot just have private groups establishing themselves, getting weapons wherever they want, and then they just say we're going to defend the country. I mean, that is chaos. And at least when President Tito was still alive and the years after this kind of chaos didn't exist, because that's why we have the laws and the laws are very clear on that and the organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, that's a helpful answer. And yet if someone does, nevertheless --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the sake of the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- violate these structures and does take up arms in defence of the country, under the constitution they are still deemed to be part of the armed forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have answered -- I'm sorry, I'm too fast. I've answered the question, that is, yes, but the but means they have to be accepted into the armed forces, into one of the elements of All People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, earlier -- well, yesterday when I asked you if someone showed up on the battle-field and they had no authorisation in the sense of the legal benediction of being in an organisation and they started participating on the battle-field or in the zone of responsibility on behalf of, as a friendly force, on behalf of or with the army, you said unequivocally that there was a duty to subordinate that individual; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think my answer was there was a duty to subordinate or to remove them. And the removal is exactly the issue of the recognition.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I apologise, but the first part of my learned friend's question at page 14, line 20, has not been recorded. And I don't know if my learned friend has channel 4 on his headphones because the interpreters were speaking at the same time as he was and I don't know if he caught that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I've turned to channel 4. I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But either way, the mere fact that they're not part of a recognised self-management organisation has no impact on the duty -- the commander's duty to either take measures to discipline and bring them into the fold, so to speak, or to exclude them from the zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to give a theoretical answer or do you want me to refer to the situation as it was in SBWS during fall 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm asking for a yes or no answer based upon your understanding of the law.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's impossible because if they're not part of an organisation that is one way or the other recognised, whether it's self-management or, as we saw, a party-affiliated volunteer group as we saw in fall 1991, they can only be recognised by the local commander if they have been recognised at a higher level. And that's why we have these various decisions that are adopted between August 1991 and December 1991 by the Republic of Serbia, the SSNO, and 10th of December the order 73 by the Presidency of SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you're saying that in that circumstance the obligation of the commander in that zone of responsibility is to eject these non-recognised persons; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if they are not recognised, yes, indeed, they should be removed. And if they commit crimes, they should be -- I mean, measures should be taken against them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if they are participating in conjunction with the zone commanders's orders and operations, that would suggest to you, would it, that that group has been accepted; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If -- I mean, I understand "in conjunction" if they are, like, identified in an order as having a task, yes, obviously then they have been accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's move on and we'll get to some concrete examples and we'll see what your answers are then. And am I right that any of these self-management organisations that are accepted, that's -- they're subject at the very top level to the SFRY Supreme Command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, based on the principle of unity and -- I mean of single and unified command and control, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And just to get a full picture of the chain of command from top to bottom, am I right in saying that the SFRY - and we're talking about 1991 under the law of the SFRY - the SFRY Supreme Command exercises that command function through the Federal Secretary of National Defence, who in turn relies on the SFRY General Staff to ensure that those orders are executed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And in the late 1980s as you described earlier and as you talked about in your report, it's right, isn't it, that Territorial Defence organisations were directly subordinated to the commands of JNA military districts; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I mean, that is the general situation and -- I mean, for specific operations obviously we have to look at specific documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let's start with just the de jure situation, Mr. Theunens, because you keep answering these caveats, qualifications, and conditions. Is what I stated correct as a matter of law?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but -- I mean -- I'm sorry that I seem to be difficult in your views, but you can find in military regulations specific military operations where a TO commander may be in command of the JNA. It depends of that -- of the tactical scenario that has to be implemented because -- I mean, this is all linked also to the nature of the TO, the TO were local troops, so if it is about defending an external aggression and, for example -- excuse me, defending against an external aggression, and then recapturing terrain that has been lost to the "aggressor," then there can be scenarios where after the main effort has been led by the JNA that the TO commander will be in command of the control of the terrain. That is a possibility. So that's why I try to be more specific in my answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But that is in no way relevant at all, is it, to the fact that the TO is subordinate to the command of the military district in which that TO is located; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean what you say is correct, but it -- again, it may be that these --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'd like to progress. I'll -- I'm in the Court's hands --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I really do not wish to cut off an expert, but I do have a line of questioning, I do have topics I want to get to. So I'm really at the Court's pleasure as to how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If it helps, you know, in general -- as a general answer I would agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, here's what you said in the Seselj case and this is at transcript 4135. This is a question from Judge Antonetti. He asked you: "So if there's one thing we should keep in mind, it's that starting in 1987 the orders forwarded to the TO go through the head of the General Staff, which was not the case before?" Answer, this is your answer: "That is correct, Your Honour, and also the TO becomes subordinated to the -- what is called the strategic operational level units, i.e., the military districts, whereas before they were on a parallel level." Do you stand by that statement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by that. And if you allow me, I try to explain because you suggested there is a difference between what I answer now and what I answered to Judge Antonetti. What I tried to say is that the general principle confined to the 1987 Jedinstvo reorganisation remains. I mean, I stand by my answer. I just want to be cautious in my answers here today because I understand we are referring to the situation as it existed in fall 1991 and subsequently in SBWS, but the general principle is the same and as I said I stand by my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And do I understand that the implication of that answer and of the Jedinstvo plan, which you referred to, was that the presidents of the republics were removed from the chain of command between the SFRY Supreme Command and the TOs in the republics; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that's true in peace and in war time; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, that is correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And an example of that was the fact that an order came down from the General Staff saying that weapons should be removed from TO depots and placed in JNA depots; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that order didn't go through the presidents of the republics, did it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't. I mean, it didn't have to because it came -- initially the instruction came from the Supreme Command, i.e., the SFRY Presidency -- I mean, the Supreme Command, sorry, had not been activated then but came -- the initial directive came from the SFRY Presidency and was accepted there by the republics, otherwise the Presidency could not have instructed the SSNO and then the General Staff to issue that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: At page 189 of your report you say: "When not participating in combat operation or operations the local Serb TO in SAO SBWS is until at least December 1991 subordinated to the local Serb police under the command of Radovan Stojicic, aka Badza." What's the -- is there any legal foundation for that claim? Let's just start with the legal foundation. Any legal foundation for that claim?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, at -- the issue -- the problem with the legal foundation is that there was no legal provision or no provision in the constitution or the -- I mean the 1974 Constitution or the 1982 All People's Defence law or any other legal or doctrinal document until late 1991 that legalised the self-declared local Serb armed structures, be it TO, be it volunteer groups, or be it police, so I mean obviously there is then no legal foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You're surely not here disputing, sir, that all participants on the Serb side accepted the SFRY law was in force on this territory throughout at least the period up until well into at least 1992 and certainly probably beyond, but let's just stick with the period prior to the arrival of UNPROFOR, that the view of all participants on the Serb side is that SFRY law continues to apply; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My personal interpretation - and I'm not a lawyer - would be that it is their interpretation of SFRY legislation. That is what they continued to adhere to because, you know, unless you can show me an article or a document that I have missed, I am not familiar with any SFRY legal or any SFRY armed forces doctrinal document that talks about the establishment of SAOs or local Serb TO units or local Serb -- and by "local Serb," I mean SAO, so Serbs in Croatia, TO or MUP units. And this creates a lot of confusion also among the JNA, as we see in the various documents, for example, from the 1st Military District during fall 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But there were the autonomous provinces of Vojvodina and Kosovo and no one would have suggested that there was any difficulty in understanding the SFRY law applied in those autonomous provinces; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the big and the key difference, Your Honours, in relation to Kosovo and Vojvodina was that at the time they were autonomous provinces, and I think one of the two was also an autonomous region at one time, that was explicitly recognised in the legal documents, the SFRY legal documents, and, for example, indeed they had their own TO, but the big difference between those TOs, i.e., Kosovo and Vojvodina and on the other hand SAO SBWS or SAO Krajina or SAO Western Slavonia is that if the TOs of Kosovo and Vojvodina were legally recognised and they existed as a structure and everybody accepted them and the JNA - I mean from the top level to the lowest level - knew that this was a legally recognised organisation and a part of the All People's Defence concept, whereas for the SAOs - as we have seen - I mean there is a document from -- I mean, there was the document by Colonel Trajkovic, the Chief of Staff of the 12th Corps asking the 1st Military District, like: What do we do with these people? And, okay, I believe we should recognise them. But it shows the confusion that exists at the level of the JNA as to what is the legal status and, therefore, what can we do or what should we do with these people, I mean by that structures of the SAO in this case SBWS. What do we do with these people and how do we treat them? So that's the big difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The difficulty I'm having with this assertion on your part, just to be clear, is that the document that you cite in support of this claim is not issued by Mr. Stojicic in the name of any police structure. The certificate is issued in the name of a TO structure. And that's why I'm asking you the question: Where do you get the conclusion that the TO is placed under the police at any time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We should -- I mean, it would be helpful if I could see the certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let's bring that up, please, that's 65 ter 794, Prosecution tab 234.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record this is Exhibit P198.140. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is correct that in this specific document there is no reference to the police. I'm trying to recall, it must have been my understanding that Badza, I mean Radovan Stojicic, had a position in the local Serb police in the SAO SBWS, but I don't have a reference here so that's what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Does that mean that you're relying on information that you haven't footnoted in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or it may have been that the footnote -- cutting and pasting or something. I will check into this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But you were a participant in many witness interviews over the years. Is it possible you heard someone say something and somehow that coloured your interpretation as expressed on page 189?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, Your Honours. It may have been that it was open-source reporting. There were some articles which are not cited here, but I think there was a JNA intelligence review article on the local Serb defence or military and police structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: As a matter of SFRY law and doctrine, does it make any sense that the TO is placed under the police?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be unusual, but I want to remind you of the various documents and decisions that are adopted in the SAO Krajina during summer 1991 and especially the role played by Mr. Martic who was not only minister of interior or becomes minister of interior and is also in charge of the SAO Krajina self-declared police but also achieves certain functions that could be or duties that could be defined as command duties even if it was de facto, I agree on that, in relation to the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, of course that -- we're not talking now about the SAO Krajina, we're talking about the SAO SBWS. And I think you'd agree in Martic's case that was a question of double-hatting; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You may call it double-hatting, but it -- I put in the Martic report and it was also my testimony that there was a power struggle between Martic and Babic which also reflected itself in who was to be in command over the TO. And there is a footnote on that issue, I mean 552, for example, on same page here in the amalgamated report, page 189.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Why don't you just take the document in front of you at face value as reflecting the situation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I agree with you -- I'm sorry. I agree with you that this certificate does not mention the police, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Not only does it not mention the police, it suggests that what we're dealing with is a Territorial Defence and that's Badza indicating that he's the one at the head of that; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you testified earlier that there was a theoretical possibility which is actually prescribed by the Law on All People's Defence for JNA units to be subordinate to TO commanders. But would you agree with me that there is no indication that that at all occurred in the area of the SBWS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean during fall 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Fall 1991 through the arrival of UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So that means that in that place and during that time-period we have the JNA being superior to the TO; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it's -- you cannot describe the situation -- I mean, it -- the complexity of the situation by just giving a yes or no answer to this very broad question --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let's stick to doctrine then, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the whole issue, Your Honours, here is about how the doctrine was applied in the area. And this is exactly why I need to refer to so many documents. If it was just a simple question of applying the doctrine, I would have given -- I mean, a ten-page report would have been sufficient. This is the doctrine and this is how it was. Sadly, the way how things went, not only in SBWS but in other parts of Croatia and later in Bosnia-Herzegovina, was not always consistent with doctrine and that's why I have done the effort to look at the specific documents and comparing the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you -- what you're suggesting here, you're reserving for yourself the possibility that you've seen documents or you've seen indications that the TO is somehow superior to JNA soldiers or units in the SBWS in 1991 and through the arrival of UNPROFOR; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- not at all, Your Honours. What I'm trying to suggest, and I just wish to refer in that context to, for example, the Panic order you brought up yesterday from the 15th of October, it's 161482-17 or -16 where he orders in very strict and very clear language JNA to remain in charge in the area of -- the area they have captured and not to abandoned -- I mean not to abandon, not to loosen control there, to stay in control because of attempts of interference of what he calls local organs of authority. This is why I put the caveat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, isn't that precisely an assertion of command and control by the JNA over TO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, but referring back to your general question to say that the JNA was always in command, well, this Panic order as well as one that he issues I think a week later shows that in some areas there have been problems and these problems are due to the fact that once the JNA has captured an area and if in a specific area combat operations as such have finished even if there is still a state of armed conflict, then there are difficulties whereby some people or groups apparently according to Panic misuse that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let's be very clear, I'm not in any way suggesting to you that there were not acts of indiscipline or that the command and control by the JNA was perfect. What I am attempting to ascertain is whether it's your view that those groups that were engaging in that indiscipline behaviour were subordinated to the JNA at the time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, maybe I can clarify -- I have documents on events in Dalj prison on I think on 21st of September, 1991, and I think the 4th of October, 1991. We can go into these documents, but the JNA is not mentioned in any of these documents and this is a typical example of what Panic tries to highlight in his order of the 15th of October. Hostilities in Dalj go back to, I believe, the 1st of August, 1991, the JNA intervenes, interposes, and then the JNA establishes de facto Serbian control over the area. There's even still during a very long time forward command post of a corps located there, but still certain acts -- and I wouldn't call it just indiscipline but crimes, at least according to the documents I reviewed, crimes occurred there. Is the JNA responsible? Well, we would -- I mean, theoretically for sure because this is -- there is a JNA unit in the area, but it doesn't -- it's not a black-and-white situation where all responsibility is focused on one organisation or one individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now you seem to be giving certain answers that do pertain to Article 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute pretty directly even though you said that that's not the scope of your expertise. In any event, let me move on. Do you think that the commander's obligation in a zone of responsibility is in any way limited by or related to combat? In other words, is there a limit defined functionally to the commander's responsibility in his zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's responsible for the force operating under his command, whatever the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And operating under his command, those words that you just used, that's broader than just a soldier sitting in a trench shooting at the other side; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question, but I assume it is one -- a soldier of one of his units or --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, my point is that -- and you've said this in previous cases, and this is the point I'm trying to get at in terms of the -- the duty to subordinate and the scope of the duty to subordinate, what I'm trying to get at here and the question I'm asking you is: Does the duty to subordinate come to an end when a soldier is not at the front line shooting at the other side?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, Your Honours, I -- my memory may fail me, but I have never used the concept "duty to subordinate" in those words. When I -- what comes the closest to "duty to subordinate" are these orders we have been discussing now, whereby SSNO 1st Military District, also the Presidency order 73, state that volunteer units operating in a zone where the JNA is have to be subordinated or removed. That is the closest to the concept to duty to subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So they have a duty to do one or the other at least, duty to subordinate or remove; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, basically it's -- because it also depends -- I mean, who has the initiative, because the order 73 talks about units that refuse to be subordinated to the JNA have to be removed, but it comes back to the same thing. So let's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if they don't remove that unit and that unit or those individuals commit a crime, is the JNA commander responsible for that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they are in his zone of responsibility, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So that's -- you're saying now - and I just want to get this very clear - you're saying it's immaterial whether or not the group is engaging in functions that are related to defence, security, combat?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, I'm trying to understand or interpret your questions in relation to the events in 1991, where obviously I mean JNA commanders -- and again this is also clear from Panic's documents, you don't necessarily need my answer, but indeed if the JNA commander fails to subordinate volunteers or whatever to his command or fails -- and if that doesn't work, fails to remove them, then he will be held accountable by in that case the commander of the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let me come straight to the point then. Was Arkan's men and Arkan himself, were they subordinated to the JNA from the time of their arrival in August 1991 through the arrival of UNPROFOR in 1992? Were they subordinated to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have seen I think one or two combat documents, orders from the 12th Novi Sad Corps indicating that during operations in Luzac, Arkan and his group operate under the command of the JNA in combat units -- in combat operations, I'm sorry. There is also -- we saw the document I think from December 1991 or January 1992 from the 12th Corps providing a status of forces, whereby it is indeed confirmed that Arkan's volunteers or TO detachment is subordinated to the JNA at that time. However, the various reports by security organs of the 1st Military District between October and -- 1991 and the course of 1992 suggest that Arkan is not always subordinated to the JNA, and even if he should have been, that he's acting on his own behalf and they attribute - I mean "they" is the 1st Military District security organs - they attribute this behaviour and the fact that he seems -- that Arkan seems to be able to get away with that to his connections with local -- I mean with the SAO SBWS authorities or even senior officials or members of the Government of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So your position is that he is stepping in and out of subordination; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's look at some documents now, and I know you want to and I'm more than happy to oblige.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06198, which is Prosecution tab 665. This is Prosecution Exhibit 1687.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you know whether that's in my report?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You mentioned it the day before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But I don't believe it is in your report, sir.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's a new document basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I just want to try to situate us tactically in this area and understand what forces are present. And this is an early document which is why I find it useful. It's from the 12th Corps. It states the date is the 8th of July, 1991, and this is from Mladen Bratic, who is the commander of the 12th Corps. And down there at paragraph 2 or item 2 it says: [As read] "I have decided the 12th Corps forces (the 51st and 452nd Mechanised Brigades and parts of the 36th Mechanised Brigade) shall advance through Slavonia in two marching columns in Slavonia and one in Baranja on the following axes ..." Now, I'm not interested in the axes as such, but can you just help us understand how many forces by establishment should be encompassed by the units that are mentioned there numerically?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to give a precise estimate because I don't know the level of mobilisation of these units. I mean, there would -- when we talk about brigades, we're talking about several thousands of troops. A brigade could be 5.000 troops or even more. But it all depends -- I mean, from here, for example, I cannot say whether these were level A, B, or C units. That was a classification that existed in the JNA to, yeah, determine I wouldn't say the importance of the unit but their level of permanent manning because some units would only exist as a skeleton in peace time and they would have to be mobilised, whereas others had a stronger peace time strength so I'm sorry I'm not able to give a precise estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What's the range?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a brigade I would say between 5- and 10.000, a mechanised brigade between 5 - and 10.000 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So we have two brigades here and parts of a third brigade so that you're talking about over 10.000?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it -- I mean it's a purely theoretical thing because on the other hand when you look at the terrain, I mean you would have a major traffic jam to try to move them over the three bridges. So I've seen estimates that there were more -- like more than 70.000 JNA troops at one given time in fall 1991 surrounding Vukovar or fighting in that area. Other estimates were 20.000. You know, I find it hard to believe that around 10.000 troops would move in July -- try to move over the three bridges over the Danube because it would be a major, yeah, logistical challenge. So I believe it's -- I would say it is less.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Attachment 1 has some interesting information. If we could go to page 5 in the English, it's the last page in B/C/S. In Eastern Slavonia -- sorry, this is an attachment which is headed "intelligence situation." There's no authorship but here is what it says: "In Eastern Slavonia: In Erdut village there is a training centre for around 300-400 members of the Croatian National Guard and MUP ..." Do you know anything about what training centre is being referred to there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's most likely the same training centre that was taken over by Arkan at one moment I think during fall 1991 and which was later transformed in a training centre for the TO of the RSK, and I think it was even at one time identified as a training centre for the special units of the TO, the special police units of the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And then a bit further down: "In all settlements snipers have been deployed on church towers and the sectors are fortified and positions consolidated for defence." Is that corroborated by other information as far as you know, namely, that there were Croatian positions being taken up in church towers?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen, Your Honours, other documents, I mean JNA documents, mentioning that, but I haven't, for example, looked at Croatian documents so there's not much I can say about it. I didn't analyse the activities of the ZNG or the Croatian forces in SBWS. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 05995, please, which is Defence tab 512.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is coming up -- while this is coming up on the screen in front of you, Mr. Theunens, this is a document, a report from the 12th Corps command by Trajkovic, the Chief of Staff, and he's describing the disposition of forces, and the date is the 22nd of September, 1991. And we see here the same units that are mentioned in the previous document, namely, the 51st and the 452nd, although I think in this document we see that it's being referred to as 453rd instead of the 452nd. And then we also see the 36th Brigade. But in addition to that we see the 18th Mechanised Brigade, the remainder of the 36th Brigade, the 12th Motorised Brigade which is now being stationed in Klis, the village of Klis which I presume is Klisa, the village of Tenja, Betin Dvor; the 211th Armoured Brigade has now been stationed in the villages of Erdut, Aljmas, Lipovac; and the 16th Mixed Artillery Regiment is based in Klisa and the Klisa Ekonomija. Now, I generally understand your difficulty in coming to a precise figure as to what -- how many people are in all these forces. Can you give us a general ballpark figure as to how many soldiers you think are comprised by these various units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm very reluctant to make a guess here because, I mean, you may have heard before in other trials that, for example, the 80th Brigade, the first attempt to mobilise it failed so they couldn't march towards Eastern Slavonia -- sorry, a second attempt, and then also the manning was still low. I can repeat the theoretical strength but I don't think it's going to bring much, so the safest I can -- guess I can make there were several thousands of JNA troops at that time in Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 00589 which is Prosecution tab 170, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this appears to be from the 1st Military District command and this is in November 1991 so it's a little bit later, reporting to the General Staff of the SFRY. And if we turn the page to page 11, it indicates that there are -- I presume these are Serbian TO units that are being attached to the 12th Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean TO of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we see 2.024.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't have the page in front of me but I'm familiar with the document, it's in my report. Yeah, I mean, it's possible, yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There is no page 11 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, in any event it's not important. I have a page 11 in my version.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But in any event that's what that document indicates. Could we have --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't want to -- but just to clarify also the issue in my answer in relation to Arkan when you said he would be coming and going, it would be interesting to see whether Arkan's unit is now mentioned on the strength of the 1st Military District because if he was subordinated at that time he and his unit would have been included in this overview.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We're progressing step by step on that issue, Mr. Theunens, but thank you for that comment.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 05997, please, which is Defence tab 320.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is the document that creates OG North; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's a new document, Your Honours. I would say it is a document that creates an OG North because I've seen the -- I mean I didn't have this document prior to -- or when the amalgamated report was put together. I spoke in during examination about the difficulties to obtain documents from the 12th Corps or OG North and we requested those already in 2003 or 2004 prior to the Vukovar trial. I was always under the understanding that there was an OG North which was based in the 12th Corps and which was commanded first by General Bratic and then when he was killed in action by General Biorcevic. This document here talks, in my view, about an OG North because it's much smaller than the initial OG North or the -- that OG North I was thinking of under the command of Biorcevic or Bratic prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Although this document does say "the Operation Group North"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but I mean because it's at that given time. It cannot say "an OG North." At that time there is only one OG North, that is this one. So as OGs and TGs are ad hoc arrangements that can be disbanded, re-established, changed, and so on, for OG North based on the documents I have reviewed, it is difficult for me to establish what the exact sequence of call it restructuring is because here we see, in my view, an OG North. There is a document a few weeks later for a Tactical Group North then only the 12th Corps is mentioned, whereas in a number of open sources, as I mentioned, mention was made of the OG North, which was a much bigger unit comparable to OG South, where the situation is much more straightforward. Again, it's easier to analyse because of the documents we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, whatever the case may be, one thing we can I think agree on is if you look at the list of units there, it includes a TO Panonic Brigade and the TO detachment of Serbia. Do you know where the Panonic TO is from?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall at this stage, but I can check. I mean, I assume it is originating from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we see there that the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Brigade is listed here in OG North but we know that they end up in the command of OG South later; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with the first proposition. For the second, I mean at one moment -- at one moment in time the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division which consists of proletarian guards mechanised brigades is deployed south of OG South, so I don't recall exactly whether a proletarian guards mechanised brigade is subordinated to OG South, but I do recall that its parent unit, i.e., the Proletarian Mechanised Division is deployed south of OG South at one moment in fall 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Item 6: "Round up all personnel and materiel by 1200 hours on 29 September 1991 on the village of Brsadin-Trpinjska Cesta- Borovo Selo axis." Can you provide us any assistance as a military man as to what the words "round up" means? What's being instructed here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just looking at what -- I mean, what I can see on the screen and given the limited information I have on the 12th Corps, I would interpret that as preparing all personnel of the mentioned units in order to be ready to act and to do that in the locations -- in the location mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is already admitted on 8th of May as P1690. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could we have 1D298, please, which is Defence tab 370.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, this is a map which purportedly was created by the Central Intelligence Agency. Have you seen this map before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and if you want I can explain more on the background of what you call the Central Intelligence Agency involvement in preparing the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I'm not particularly interested in that, but is there something you can tell us briefly on that subject?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just to clarify -- I mean when people hear "Central Intelligence Agency," they often think of -- that clandestine and covert sources were used to prepare this information. Basically, I mean this is part of a quite detailed report called: "Balkan Battlegrounds on the Conflict in the former Yugoslavia," but it's all based on open sources. Nothing wrong with open sources, but just to clarify potential misunderstandings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we know from the documents that we've just looked at that they seem to have gotten correct a good number of the units that they've got identified there on the map in the area of OG North. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be helpful if maybe the map can go down a bit and I can see the date. I think there must be a date somewhere maybe on the top or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If you look closely at the legend there, you'll see that the inner lines of confrontation were allegedly reached according to this on the 30th of September, 1991.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, mm-hmm. Okay. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But the general question is: Would you agree with me that they have accurately represented the units that, based on the documents, appear to be there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I have no reason to doubt about what they are saying, but from an analytical point of view and a methodological point of view, I would first like to see their figures because I see only like icons of units. And then compare that -- I mean their findings with my material and then draw conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And looking at this map, can we just get an overview of the operations that occurred in OG North, starting on the 1st of August? We've heard a lot of evidence that they crossed the bridge on the 1st of August, they moved into Erdut and Dalj. We'll go to certain documents on that, but let me ask you this specifically: Do you know that they reached that confrontation line, the inner confrontation line, almost immediately once they had crossed the bridges, based on the documents you've looked at?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What -- excuse me, what do you mean by "inner confrontation line"?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: By "inner," I mean the dotted line.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. You know, I cannot compare it -- I can read the map and I have no reason to doubt about the accuracy of this map in relation to the information the analysts or the people who compiled this map had available to them. From my point of view as well as I answered earlier, I would like to look at the documents I have, I mean the official JNA documents which were not available to the people who drafted or compiled this map and then compare the two, and then I could answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that OG North is separated from OG South until well into October, as seems to be reflected on this map?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- it's possible -- I mean, it's possible, yeah. It's what the -- sorry, it's what the map seems to show. But again, I cannot draw that conclusion from the documents I have reviewed, so I can draw that conclusion only -- I mean, I can answer your question based on the map I see in front of me and my understanding -- because apparently -- I mean, there is the Vuka river between the two, but -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We would tender this map, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D38. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could I have Prosecution Exhibit -- sorry, P1688, Defence -- Prosecution tab 666.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is the -- a report from the Chief of Staff of the command of the 12th Corps dated the 9th of August, 1991, to the command of the 1st Military District, General Mladen Maksimovic. And it purports to describe the events in or around Dalj on the 1st of August, 1991. Can I first of all ask you about the interval. Is it normal that there would be an interval of eight days between a combat action and a report of this type?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it doesn't say "regular situations report," so I don't know whether the 12th Corps prior to the 9th of August was providing regular situation reports to the 1st Military District. This seems to be a kind of a summarising or an overview report, so I would want to check first whether other situation reports were sent or submitted by the 12th Corps to the 1st Military District between the 1st of August and the 9th of August. Maybe we should have -- would also look at the war diary of the 12th Corps which unfortunately was not accessible to me and then I would be able to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's say there were daily ongoing situation reports, why would there be a report like this even if there were those types of reports?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe because the commander or a member of the command of the 1st Military District asked the 12th Corps to provide such report, we don't know. I don't consider it unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's go over to page 2 of the English, please. "A tactical company of the 2nd Armoured Battalion started out across the bridge and crossed it without having to open fire. During this time, a white flag was put out on the 'Kula' installation in the village of Erdut and ZNG members withdrew from the elevation." Let's just stop there for a moment. Do you know of any elevations in the town of Dalj?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Erdut or Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Erdut. Do you know of any elevations in the village of Erdut?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean if I remember well, because I've been there for the last time it's like 1997, when you cross -- I mean, if you come from Serbia across the bridge, close to the bridge there is I think kind of elevation but it's not very big. I mean overall the terrain in Eastern Slavonia is flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can an elevation be a building in military parlance?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen it, you know, I -- if it's a building, you would expect that it's described as a building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It goes on: "Then a tactical company of the 1st Motorised Battalion was sent across the village of Dalj at 07:30 hours followed by a tactical company of the 2nd mb, which headed towards the village of Erdut after crossing the bridge but came under strong fire from the direction of the MUP centre. "As a result this unit was forced to return fire and prevent the ZNG from firing upon them. "At 09:30 hours a tactical company of the 1st mb entered the village of Dalj and once it was there the unit commander asked the warring parties through a spokesperson to cease firing ... both sides agreed except for the forces positioned at the MUP station. Since these forces continued firing not only on the other side but on the tactical company of the 1st mb as well, they were given an ultimatum to cease firing right away or tanks would be deployed to destroy them. Despite the ultimatum and several warnings, forces positioned at the MUP station continued firing on units of the 1st mb which was forced to return fire and three shells from a tank gun were fired on the police station, after which the conflict between the warring parties stopped and no more fire was opened on units of the 1st mb. "Under the protection of our units members of the MUP and the ZNG then retreated towards the village of Aljmas and some were evacuated to Osijek together with the refugees, also under the protection of JNA units." Now, you testified that there was a shift in JNA -- in the JNA's role in the conflict in 1991 from separating the sides to then actively participating on one side against the other. Is this, in your view, a clear indication of participating on one side against the other?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that -- at this stage it's - and I think it's indicated in the report, according to the report the main role of the JNA consists of separating the parties and, as is put in this report, enforcing a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, here's my point, sir. On page 1 of this report the author is giving the impression that this is a matter of the JNA separating the two sides acting as an honest broker, so to speak, but then when you get into the details, namely, a tank moves in, destroys the MUP station, presumably killing a large number of people, isn't that participating on one side against the other at that point?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the best I can answer is that it depends of the -- which side you're on. For the Croatian side obviously it means that the JNA by separating the parties and actually consolidating Serbian control over certain areas is actually participating on the Serbian side of the conflict. For the JNA, as you can see in this document, it means separating the parties and using all necessary means to enforce or impose a cease-fire. For myself, I think this document leaves room for interpretation. Subsequent documents are much clearer as to the role of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Theunens, time for the first break. We'll come back at 11.00. The court usher will escort you out of the courtroom. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [The witness takes the stand].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, before the break you were disputing my interpretation of this document as a crossing of the Rubicon I would say of the JNA towards actively participating in this conflict on the Serb side. Now, let me direct you to the bottom of the page that's on the screen there, where it says, if we can go down a little bit more in the English: "The MUP and ZNG units stationed in the villages of Dalj and Erdut were the ones that caused the conflict with the JNA unit." Notwithstanding the higher aspirations of the JNA to act as policemen between the two sides, wouldn't you agree with me that this is in reality reflecting a shift towards acting on one side against the other, regardless of the reasons?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I don't know. I mean, I read the sentence according to the command of the 12th Corps indeed -- I mean, he states that the MUP and ZNG units caused the conflict with the JNA. If we were to analyse the attitude of the each of the parties at that moment in the conflict, we would also have to look at documents from the Croatian side, I mean if that was the purpose of our analysis, and then try to form an opinion on that. As I said earlier, to me this document leaves room for interpretation and there are documents -- later documents from various JNA units that are much clearer. At the same time, when you look at documents concerning the situation in Banija, Kordun, and Lika, for example, with the various OGs and TGs that are set up, some of them as already as early as September, there it is clear that the JNA is fighting on the Serbian side. The same happens in the wider Knin area that's around the same time-period. But I understood that you wanted to give me an interpretation based on this specific document, and there I have tried to do that to my -- to the best of my abilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The paragraph above that says: "The unit also did not enter the village of Dalj during the day ..." But then a few paragraphs up it says. "At 09:30 hours a tactical company of the 1st mb entered the village of Dalj ..." Why do you think Trajkovic isn't being entirely honest here?
