utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't understand the reference to whether Mr. Trajkovic is honest or not. You could try to analyse Mr. Trajkovic's honesty or lack thereof of if you would have independent observers in Dalj who could express their views in relation to the views expressed by Mr. Trajkovic or Colonel Trajkovic and then, yes, you could draw conclusions. Maybe he's dishonest, maybe not. You know, I can't make that -- draw any conclusions to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Last paragraph on this page: "In the days after the conflict there were occasional incidents between the Croatian and Serbian inhabitants and our units (mostly the military police) entered the village of Dalj to prevent acts of retaliation against the Croatian population." Now, can you discern in this document that Trajkovic seems to be sensitive or concerned about as of when or what date his forces are in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the date of the document, I think it's from 1st of September, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No, it's from the 9th of August.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, 9th of August, I couldn't see that at the top of the document. I mean, linked to that paragraph it would suggest in the days after the 9th of August units of the -- I mean military police of the 12th Corps enters Dalj, but it doesn't state how long they stay, whether they establish a permanent presence or whether they go in and leave again. So we would have to look at other documents from the 12th Corps to see the -- their deployment at any given time during that time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Last paragraph of the document which is on page 3: "We believe that the situation in the settlement of Dalj is still very complex due to the mistrust that has been created there. Both warring parties believe that JNA presence is necessary and useful and that in the present situation the withdrawal of JNA forces would have disastrous consequences." So someone is providing Trajkovic with information on the situation in the town; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the paragraph shows that Trajkovic expresses his assessment of the situation in Dalj. What this is based on, we cannot establish from this document, but it would be reasonable to assume that he is gathering information and obtaining information on the situation in Dalj at that moment in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No mention in this document, is there, of any participation by Arkan in this event; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which event, Your Honours, because it's a summarising report?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: "Report on the armed conflict near the village of Dalj."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no mention is made of Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No mention of Arkan in any of the three previous documents that we looked at setting out the forces that were part of the 12th Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Even though those documents also listed certain TO units that were to be attached to the 12th Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you said earlier today that that would be to you -- or you would look to those documents in order to determine whether or not Arkan is subordinated to JNA forces as of this date; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes in the sense that the mentioning of Arkan among the own units would indicate that at that moment in time Arkan is subordinate and his group are subordinated to the JNA. As we see from 1st Military District security organs documents, the JNA units also report about the presence of Arkan or other volunteer groups in certain parts of SBWS even if they are not -- even if they do not appear to be subordinated to the JNA at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's at a later time-period and we're coming to that. I want to focus on August 1991, and you said earlier that you would look to these types of documents to determine whether Arkan was or was not subordinated to the 12th Corps at this time. So my question to you is: Does the absence of mention in this document and the previous documents inform your view - and I believe this is your view but please tell if it's otherwise - your view that in August 1991 Arkan is not subordinated to the 12th Corps in this area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. I mean, based on the documents we have seen and the absence of any mention of Arkan and his group in these documents, Arkan is not -- and his group are not subordinated to the 12th Corps at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's have P103, please, Prosecution tab 93. This is an information signed by Colonel Stevan Mitrevski who apparently is part of a logistics sector of some unit, and this report has gone up -- you've discussed it before. This unit has gone to very high levels, security administration of some units, the Federal Secretariat for -- I believe the security administration of the Federal Secretariat for National Defence at least and other units. And down at the bottom of page 1 we see information relating back to the initial arrival of the 12th Corps in Erdut and it says: "He said that using explosive Arkan had completely destroyed a Catholic church in the village of Erdut and the church tower was destroyed before that during the JNA take-over of Erdut." No mention of that in Trajkovic's report, is there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Would the information in this report be salient to your analysis of whether or not Arkan is subordinated to the 12th Corps at this place and at that time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I mean, with the break -- could you remind me the date of the Trajkovic document we looked at?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's the 9th of August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, well, this document is dated the 1st of October so -- I mean we can -- we can objectively state that there is no reference in Trajkovic's document dated the 9th of August, but we don't know why there is no mention.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Are you disputing that the last sentence on page 1 of this document means to refer to the take-over of Erdut on the 1st of August by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not disputing that, but I just compared the two documents like anybody would do that here information is mentioned that is not mentioned in the other document. That's all I can observe or state at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you mention that in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because as we saw I didn't have the Trajkovic document available to me and I -- I assume from -- I mean when I was checking the internet on the status of the report I compiled in October, that the Defence was quite negatively oriented towards the second report, so again I cannot analyse documents that I don't physically have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How does this information in this report, now that I have drawn it to your attention, affect, if at all, your assertion that Arkan is not subordinated to the 12th Corps in this area at this time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a doctrinal point of view, Arkan should have been subordinated to the 12th Corps during their operations in Erdut. However, when we look at the context and all the other military documents, the situation is not entirely clear. We do know that Arkan develops a good relationship with the future or the later commander of the 12th Corps, namely, General Biorcevic. I haven't been able to review sufficient documents of the 12th Corps to establish the nature of his relations at the moment when units of the 12th Corps take over Erdut. But again, from a theoretical point of view there should have been subordination and there should have been co-ordination in their activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You testified at page 4183 of this case a couple of days ago that you had made requests for documents from the 12th Corps and that you had received very few documents. Now, am I correct in understanding that you've received far fewer documents from -- in relation to the area of responsibility of the 12th Corps as compared to documents in relation to the area of responsibility of OG South?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you explain that? Why is there that difference?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- no, Your Honours, I cannot explain. I think maybe the country or the -- I think the states holding these documents, they are in a much better to -- position to explain than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Have you -- do you have personal knowledge of documents in archives being destroyed or concealed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: An argument that was often heard and I'm -- I mean I don't recall specifically in which -- whether it was in the context of which request, but that a number of documents held in archives in FRY were destroyed during the bombing, aerial bombing, conducted by NATO in the context of the operations in Kosovo in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What I meant by my question which I guess could have been clearer: Intentionally destroying in order to conceal events?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but again maybe it's not an answer to your question but just for the -- it can assist the Trial Chamber. When I was working on the Vukovar case, we submitted requests for similar documents at different times. And documents that were, for example, reportedly unavailable at one moment suddenly were available four months later. Now, whether there was a particular intention to that or whether it was due to lack of organisation, I don't know. Or we would request documents and then we obtained totally different documents. But that was the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Have you ever come across a document that you were able to ascertain was forged that had been provided to you from any source that was purporting to be a JNA document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a few documents -- and again, I can only talk about the documents that I saw. But there were a few documents I think related to the JNA 2nd Military District or obtained from state archives in Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time where there was certain doubts about their authenticity. And -- I mean, these documents had nothing to do with Eastern Slavonia -- the situation in Eastern Slavonia or SBWS. I understood from my colleagues that they undertook efforts to verify the authenticity from these documents, for example, by showing them to JNA officers during witness or suspect interviews and that matter was then clarified afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, JNA officers who themselves might have an interest in engaging in that forgery; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I mean, those particular cases I would consider doubtful because these documents were quite negative, hostile towards -- about the JNA or towards the JNA and its activities during spring 1992 in the wider Sarajevo area or in Bosnia-Herzegovina. So -- and they all came from the same archive and they had this -- I mean, it was all like for specific time-period -- it was almost like sensational kind of information that was included, and referring to the methodology one had certain doubts about the reliability of the source, not so much the source indicated on the document but the provider of the document and the layout of the document and on the other hand the contents. So then you apply the methodology.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Have you ever come across a document in relation to the SBWS region that you would say has been tampered with?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And by -- just to clarify my question, by "tampered with," I mean someone after the creation of the document has altered its content for whatever reason?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will qualify my answer, I mean I -- to the best of my recollection I haven't seen any documents originating from the 1st Military District or its subordinate units where there are indications that the document has -- the content of the document has been altered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What about the war diary of the Guards Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again based on -- I was I think I find privileged to be involved in the interview of the drafter of the war diary. And just also to clarify one of your questions yesterday, the JNA officers I -- when I say "I interviewed," when I participated in the interview by the investigator, most of those became Defence witnesses. So it was not just a matter of collecting information that was favourable to the Prosecution or, as you suggested earlier, that I would be influenced by views that were favourable to the Prosecution. But as I mentioned, I participated in the interview of that officer. That officer also testified. And I'm not aware of any reservations being raised during or after the Vukovar trial by any witness or any other individual in relation to the authenticity of the war diary of the Guards Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is it credible there could be no mention of the evacuation agreement of Vukovar Hospital in that war diary?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know whether it was in his testimony in front of the Trial Chamber or during his interview that one of the drafters of the -- I mean the one we interviewed and at this moment -- I mean I can find his name back but I don't recall his name. He said that, well, you know, once, I mean, we had the 18th of November and Vukovar had "fallen," people became a bit sloppy in their -- in the reporting and the war diary was not kept to the same level of discipline as before. So, again based on that and on the absence of any similar objections as the ones you raise now, the absence during the trial and afterwards, I have no reason to believe that the war diary of the Guards Motorised Brigade has been tampered with. I would agree with the fact that it's -- it lacks maybe comprehensiveness is not the right word but it appears to be incomplete. Events happening after the 18th are not covered with the same level of detail as it should have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Are you seriously suggesting that those omissions are a matter of mere sloppiness?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not suggesting anything. To the best of my ability I tried to answer the question and reflect the views that have been expressed by me by those -- I mean by people who have drafted the document and also the one who is actually -- I mean, the Chief of Staff of the Guards Motorised Brigade who was responsible for the contents. So he supervised the drafting of the war diary and this is what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I mean, isn't it an obvious example of a JNA document being written in such a way to avoid responsibility for certain events?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is possible, I don't know, but looking at military doctrine and also the military discipline and justice system, a war diary as such would not be sufficient to establish responsibility or the lack thereof or avoid responsibility in a kind of situation as the one that occurred in Ovcara on the afternoon and the evening of the 20th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, the individuals involved in -- I apologise for the absence of a gap. The individuals involved in keeping that war diary aren't being contemporaneously advised by lawyers on that surely?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I mean I've answered the question. You know, it's not just an issue of the war diary. There's also other documents that -- allow to establish who is in command of who and who is responsible for what.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's get back to Dalj, see whether or not Trajkovic's report is accurately reflecting events.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 892, Prosecution tab 246.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm sure you're familiar with this document, Helsinki Watch to Milosevic dated the 21st of January, 1992. If we go to page 3 in the English, please, under the entry "August 1st Dalj." And here's what Helsinki Watch is reporting. If we can go to the next page in English, please. It seems we have B/C/S on both sides. [As read] "On August 1, Serbian insurgents attempted to take over the local police station in Dalj. Police trapped inside the station refused to surrender to JNA troops and a battle for the town ensued. After the JNA occupied Dalj, Serbian paramilitary troops reportedly searched the village for Croatian soldiers, police officers, and civilians, and killed many of those who were found wounded." Now, you notice that this document, Mr. Theunens, says that the JNA occupied Dalj, whereas Mr. Trajkovic seems extremely insistent that his forces didn't occupy Dalj on the 1st of August; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- I mean comparing the two documents, I would agree with your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Which do you think is more reliable?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean as an analyst I would say, you know, I can't answer the question now. I would look for additional information. And again, I mean the report we saw, the Trajkovic report we saw, was a summarising report and it's not always easy to follow the chronology because there's very few dates mentioned in it but it mainly discusses events of several days I think, whereas here we have a discussion of apparently an event on one day. It doesn't say so much whether the occupation -- it seems that it occurs on the 1st, it could also be the subsequent days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's now, if we could, go back to 356, we were just looking at this document, it's Prosecution tab 93 also known as P103. If we can go to page 2. And it's the second-last paragraph there. "There is a rumour among the JNA members located in that area that Arkan goes into the action only after the JNA units mop-up the area and then he ... and that area and commits crimes. They think that Arkan is doing it with a full support of the SDB of Serbia." Now, is that description of the participation of -- the method of participation by Arkan, isn't that consistent with what's being described in the Helsinki Watch report that we just looked at, which for the record is 00892?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's have 00235, please, which is D27, and that's Defence tab 380. And if we can turn the page to page 4 in the English and in the B/C/S it's immediately after the chart or the table. And, sir, I'm sure you're familiar with this document. This is a request by Arkan for compensation for one of his men apparently. And it says: "This is to certify that Nenad Markovic ...," et cetera, "participated in the liberation of Tenja as a member of our unit which fought in co-operation with the JNA and we emphasize that he was seriously wounded while carrying out the combat task." Do you know that information to be reliable based on the other documents you've reviewed, not with respect to this specific individual but that, A, there were JNA operations there; and B, that Arkan participated?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I've -- don't recall seeing other documents on operations in Tenja specific, so -- otherwise the document seems fine with me. So I could only answer your question if I would see other documents concerning the operations in Tenja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It goes on: "On 2 August 1991 he was transported in an army vehicle to the Sombor hospital, where he had an operation. "On 7 August ... he was transferred to the VMA in Belgrade where his left lower leg was amputated." So we have somebody who is apparently wounded on the 2nd in an operation with the JNA. He's then transported in a JNA ambulance away from the front line and then he's treated at a JNA hospital. What does that tell you about subordination, if anything, of Arkan's forces in this area at this time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically nothing because, again looking at the doctrine they should have been if -- sorry, if Arkan and his group were operating in the area where the JNA was conducting operations in accordance with doctrine they should have been subordinated to Arkan -- to -- excuse me, to the JNA. But the fact that somebody 's evacuated in a military vehicle and transported to a military hospital does not give any indication of subordination relation at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It could be that right now we're having a terminological problem because what I understand you to be saying when you say that he's not subordinated, do I understand you to say that he's not -- well, let me simply ask you: What is your view -- how are you using the term "subordination" in the last answer?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you used the word "subordination," so I answered your question. It means that when -- that Arkan and his group when they were conducting activities there, that they were conducting activities that had been ordered to them or that they had been ordered to do by the JNA. That is what I understand under subordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you don't find the fact that they're engaging in combat at the same place as the JNA and that this document is claiming that it was in co-operation with JNA, you don't find that in any way probative or indicative of the issue of the issue of subordination as you've used it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I would look -- I mean from the doctrinal point of view, he should have been subordinated, there is no doubt. However, I would want to look at other documents and, for example, the orders that the -- the written or the orders that determined the mission of the various JNA units and subordinate units in the area of Tenja in order to see whether Arkan and his unit are identified as one of these subordinate units and what their task was. I don't say that it's hundred per cent sure that he was not subordinate, that's not my claim. My answer is -- or that's not my answer. My answer is this document does not allow to draw hundred per cent clear conclusion given the context of the other documents I have looked at which show that the situation is quite complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But the absence of a formal order of subordination doesn't mean that he's not subordinated; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, not necessarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So "subordination" is a concept that can be analysed in terms of what's actually happening on the ground in terms of co-ordination of forces, executing orders, and so forth; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If two units have to co-ordinate, it doesn't mean that one is subordinate to the other. It means, however, that there is a third entity or command level involved to which these -- at least one of these two units is subordinated because, for example, you have to co-ordinate between neighbouring units but they may have a different superior and executing orders, indeed, involves subordination. You execute orders because you are subordinated to somebody.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I shouldn't have used the word "co-ordination" because I know that's a term of art in military parlance. Let's say in layman's terms if they're acting together with the JNA forces, isn't that indicative, probative of, not necessarily conclusive, indicative of subordination?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree, Your Honours, and again we would try to look at additional documents and the kind of documents I mentioned earlier in order to establish with the highest degree of accuracy, highest possible degree of accuracy what the relations between the units is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 05993, please, Defence tab 378.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is a -- again, another Trajkovic document as the Chief of Staff of the 12th Corps command, dated the 21st of September to the 1st Military District command, and there's a lot in this document, Mr. Theunens, that I would like to discuss with you. And then just to let you know where I'm going with all this, I'm then going to come back to Arkan specifically. But there's just a few general situational issues that I'd like to ask you about in this report first. It says under -- under the heading there: "Pursuant to your order, strictly confidential ... of 6 August 1991, we are hereby submitting to you the situation report as follows ..." Now, we were discussing this earlier, this sentence seems to imply that there has been an order from the 1st Military District for situation reports. How often are situation reports supposed to be submitted, given this particular circumstance?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will depend of the orders that have been given. Looking at the OG South documentation covering the time-period of its existence that was available to me, their regular situation reports were submitted on a daily basis each evening between 1800 and 2000, but it would have been explained in the orders for the 1st Military District for the operations in the area because there is a paragraph on -- it's not called communications, but there is a paragraph on the location of the command post and also on the frequency of -- for the submission of regular and extraordinary situation reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Under the situation in the units, it describes the fact that they're carrying out operations deployment according to the mission assigned to them for the forthcoming operations. Is "operations deployment" a term of art in military parlance; and if so, can you help us understand what it means?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my understanding -- I mean, I don't recall any use of this -- of the words in this combination, but I mean operations and deployment, but my understanding is that it's -- operation -- deployment in preparation of further operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And it says the 12th Corps command has come out to the command post in the area of PG, the Dalj village." Is "come out" a term of art in military parlance or does this just mean that they temporarily arrived and had a meeting with the commanders listed and that's what occurred?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, this is one of the new documents. I reviewed it but I didn't have the opportunity -- I mean, I reviewed it in September/October 2012, but I didn't have the opportunity to look at it with a language assistant because when I -- I mean, looking at it now I would ask a language assistant to check the B/C/S with me and then we would discuss it. We know that the 12th Corps establishes a command post, it could have been a forward command post, in Dalj village. At this moment I don't recall exactly when, but I believe it was prior to the 21st of September, 1991. Now, not everybody -- not the whole command is present at a forward command post, so it could be that the remainder part of the 12th Corps has indeed come to that forward command post, that's a possible interpretation, but I don't know whether maybe the translators can clarify the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's fine. And then we see discussion of TO units and that starts on page 1. It says: "The TO units which have already been deployed and are now abandoning their positions without authorisation, thereby leaving units alone in the combat formation, represent a particular problem ..." And then if we turn the page and go over to page 2. "All the TO units of the autonomous province of Vojvodina and the Republic of Serbia which make part of the forces of the 12th Corps have almost completely abandoned their positions and gone back. They are not units, but a mob behaving in a really arrogant and undisciplined way, looting property and houses, which has a negative effect on the morale among our units and the people watching that." Now, are we clear that these TO units being referred to in this report, they're subordinate to the 12th Corps in this area at this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Down at point 3 -- just to follow-up on that, it follows from that that the JNA has a duty to prosecute any crimes committed by those subordinated TO members; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I agree with your proposition, but I think it's best to use more specific language; that is, that indeed in accordance with the procedures or the doctrine -- or no, sorry, the regulations for military discipline and military justice and the 1988 regulations on the implementation of the laws of war, the JNA should, indeed, have at least reported these activities and have them investigated. And when I mean reported, not just in a regular situation report but also specific reports on the actual events and incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's go to page 103 of your report. We don't need to bring that up. This is just your reference, Mr. Theunens. And this sets out Article 1 of the Law on Military Courts. And Article 1 of that law says: "Military courts as regular courts try criminal acts committed by military persons." Now, the question is: Are these subordinated TO soldiers military persons and is that why there is JNA jurisdiction over them?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are -- I mean, I agree again with what you say, but just to be precise there is SFRY armed forces jurisdiction over them. From this document we don't know which measures the 12th Corps has undertaken, have they informed the military prosecutors -- I mean, have investigations taken place with security organs, military police --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- that wasn't my question. I'm not blaming the JNA at this point. I'm not blaming you. I'm not blaming anyone. Just a simple factual question about the interpretation of this provision.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Does military persons -- because it's not self-evident, but does "military persons" encompass TO soldiers while -- who commit crimes while subordinated to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And sorry to be more again specific, but it's recognised TO units and, okay, TO of Vojvodina and Serbia, recognised TO units, so there's no -- I mean, I agree with your proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to go back to our long earlier discussion. I'm just going to leave it there in respect of this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, further down the page there's something -- a description here that you as a military person might be able to help us understand because I as a lay person don't understand what's going on. Under 3(a) it says: "The units of MUP and ZNG are being prepared and they are active from the fortified buildings and bunkers, which makes the carrying out of combat operations more difficult, without a detailed search of the terrain and facilities at the rear of the combat formation." Now, why would the presence of opposing enemy forces in fortified buildings and bunkers have anything to do with conducting a detailed search of the terrain and facilities at the rear of the combat formation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, ideally we would have a map in order to see the deployment of the JNA and the intelligence assessment concerning the deployment or the locations where ZNG and MUP are included in these fortified buildings and bunkers because then I think it would be easier for me to answer the question. Because it -- one option could be -- but maybe this is speculative, that is, that -- I mean the JNA is arriving there, deploying, and at the same time there are certain buildings, apparently of a not specific military nature, where members of the ZNG and the Croatian Ministry of Interior are allegedly present. And perhaps these buildings are located in the rear area, i.e., the part of the zone of operation of the JNA where -- I mean, not combat operations are taking place but where their logistic support units and so on are located. I mean, not everybody is obviously on the front line. Logistical support, communication centres, and similar units and facilities are located in depth because they are otherwise exposed to hostile activities, so that could be an explanation but ideally we would have a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And providing security to forces in the depth is vitally important to combat operations; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to prevent -- I mean enemy infiltration and enemy disruption of your logistical support.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How do you define "infiltration"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Entering -- sorry. Entering without being authorised to do so and with hostile intentions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Are there concerns by the JNA at this time-period that the Croatian civilians have hostile intentions towards JNA units in this area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where civilians are mentioned in the report --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'm not asking you about this document, just to clarify. I'm asking you in general based on your review of documents.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my answer would be as follows. The JNA doesn't recognise the MUP or the ZNG and often in documents talk about Croatian paramilitary formations, i.e., illegal formations that use military structure -- have a military structure or use military techniques or tactics to conduct actually military activity. And even they use the term Ustashi. So I think -- I mean, so there is no clear recognition of combatants on the Croatian side and this also creates suspicion towards any Croatian including, I mean, civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So the answer is yes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer could be yes but it's -- I think -- I mean, it's too general. You know, we have to look at the specific document, but if it makes you -- I mean I would say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Item 6: "In the zone of responsibility of the 12th Corps, the security organs established contact with the security organs of the TO and the police in Dalj. Following a notification from the Dalj defence staff that they discovered that a radio transmitter was active in the immediate vicinity of the command post, the military police organs carried out a detailed search of the terrain and houses for which they had some leads that they had a radio transmitter. The search did not uncover anything." Now, throughout your report you use an expression when describing TO units you say "local Serb TO." Can you help us understand why you use that particular expression, local Serb TO, when you're talking about TO units in the SBWS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I use the expression "local Serb TO" or "self-established local Serb TO" or "SAO TO" because this is not the regular TO of the Republic of Croatia as it existed under the system of All People's Defence. So these are self-established units, and the documents -- I mean now talking about SBWS, the JNA military documents show that there is some confusion as to the legal status of these units. However, in other documents these SAO or local TO units are considered TO units as such by JNA commanders. So there is no standard view on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And when you say self-established - and the Chamber has heard plenty of evidence on this already, so I don't want to belabour the point for too long - but when you say "self-established," do I understand correctly that these are essentially units that are being created at the town level initially as village guards and then many of them declare themselves to be TO units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- I mean, there are certain units like that. There are others in areas where there was a Serb majority prior to the conflict where the Croats leave or they are kicked out or whatever and the Serbs take over the existing structures. And -- I mean, this is for example discussed on pages 182 and following. In different parts of Croatia with a significant Serb presence we see that such units are established and even attempts are made to create some kind of a structure with staffs at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And given the situation described in this document, given the security needs of the JNA that you've described in respect of units that are there, given the fact that local TO units are -- well, just that, they're locals, they've been there for a long time, does any of that suggest to you that the JNA is going to rely on the local Dalj TO to assist them in discharging these security tasks?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, but one doesn't necessarily imply the other. And again, when I say "local, "I say "local Serb TO units," because the "local" refers to Serb, not to TO. These are -- these units consist, as far as I remember from the documents I reviewed, almost exclusively of Serbs or maybe some non-Serbs, i.e., the people considered "loyal." Obviously it is useful for the JNA to rely on the regional knowledge of these units, but on the other hand - and again I refer to the documents that I mentioned in my report - there are instances where members of these units take, for example, Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica local Serb TO units and JNA documents, sorry, OG South, they are called TO detachments, that they are involved in acts of -- I mean, lack of discipline and even criminal behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the JNA unit in the area is directly subordinating those local TO units; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've answered that before. They should do so. Now, the key issue then comes -- I mean, they should do so during combat operations. The key issue is what happens when there are no operations anymore. This is not so much a matter for OG South because their operations continue until -- I mean, Vukovar falls on the 18th but then there are still resistance pockets that have to be dealt with and the structures that have been defined, i.e., OG South continues to exist until the 23rd of November, but for other parts of Eastern Slavonia, like, for example, Dalj, where after the initial, call it separation of forces and take-over, the areas under JNA control, there the situation is more complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You know, Mr. Theunens, this is why at the very beginning of the cross-examination I asked you so many questions about your definition of zones of responsibility, and I specifically asked you whether you had any functional limitation that would qualify the territorial definition of the zone of responsibility. And now for the first time, I believe, you're introducing this concept that the duty - and I will use the term if you don't want to - the duty to subordinate is somehow confined by what the TO units are doing in the area. Do you have an answer to that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- I have -- maybe I wasn't clear in my answer. During combat operations led by the JNA, the TO units should be under the command of the JNA. That's the doctrine and I stand by that answer. Once combat operations are finished, I say the situation is more complex, I don't say that the TO is not subordinated anymore to the JNA, that's not my answer. But we have to look at the specific documents because we see, for example, in parts of Eastern Slavonia where there are no more operations, I mean the events in Dalj 21st of September, 4th of October, there is still a JNA presence there for sure, the 12th Corps still has a command post there, but incidents occur and no mention is made of the JNA. This can mean several things. Now, from a doctrinal point of view the JNA commander will still -- in the area of Dalj will still be held responsible, but the responsibility will -- I mean, the - how you call it? - the actual case of military discipline or justice proceedings, the situation will be taken in -- the nature of the situation will be taken into account in a sense whether or not combat operations formally subordinating the TO to the JNA were ongoing or not. And just to finish, the Panic orders, 15th of October and there is also one of November, clearly state that the JNA remains in command and is responsible for what is happening and shouldn't leave an area out of control of the JNA. So I think -- I mean, this is as specific as I can be, and I think it's good to be specific given the complexity of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, when do combat operations stop according to you in the area of OG North? And when I say "OG North," I'm referring to that map that we looked at and the area in the -- to the north of the corridor separating OG North from OG South. When, according to you, just so I can understand your position, Mr. Theunens, when according to you are there combat operations in that area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, ideally, we would look at the documents and -- because they will explain, I mean the regular situation reports, the orders for combat operations, they will clearly state when operations start, when they end, which objectives are achieved, when, and how, and who participated and whatever resubordination of units may have taken place. My interpretation overall is that these operations -- I mean, for example, for Dalj, the JNA takes over control of Dalj, I think that was the 1st of August we saw, that quite soon the JNA has achieved control over the municipality of Dalj because otherwise they wouldn't put a first -- a forward command post there, it wouldn't make sense. And then we would have to look at other municipalities, so it's -- I cannot give a categorical answer because other parts of OG North or units that are sometimes -- at one moment in time part of the OG North but then continue to operate as part of the 12th Corps, well, they continue to operate to conduct combat operations towards Vukovar until at least the 18th of November, so we have to look at specific documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Notwithstanding the need to look at specific documents, I'm not sure I understand your position. If a TO unit from Serbia is present in Dalj on September 15th, the town has been in the JNA control for a good six weeks, it's about 10 kilometres from the front line with Borovo Naselje, it's about 20 kilometres from the front line with Tenja, is there a duty to -- again, I keep using my terminology and I apologise that, but you know what I'm saying --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- is there a duty to subordinate and discipline those TO units from Serbia for starters?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, I have answered the question. According to doctrine there should be, according to the orders of the 1st Military District there should be, that's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And does the same apply to the local TO units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the local Serb TO units you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same applies to them. But of course -- I mean, you could -- I mean the TO of the Republic of Serbia, you can still remove them. With the local Serb TO it becomes more complicated because if these are people from that village it's a bit of a challenge for the JNA to remove them, and then I think there would be difficulties with the SAO SBWS authorities, whereby as we see from the documents the attitude that needed to be adopted towards them is not clear either, so it was a bit of a challenging situation for a JNA commander, but the fact that there is a challenge doesn't reduce his responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Now, going back to page 1, and this is the part that I say is extremely relevant to Arkan, down at the bottom of paragraph or section (a) it says: "All the garrisons are working in an organised fashion on the induction and on dealing with the September contingent of soldiers." Now, what do you think that means?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it means that there were still conscript service in what remained of SFRY and that -- so young men were called up to do their military service, at regular times they were called up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So these are JNA conscripts not volunteers?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that would -- they would be JNA conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D39. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 343 which is Prosecution tab 89, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is a document by someone named Lieutenant -- for the Lieutenant-Colonel Ivan Metosevic [phoen] who may have something to do with -- well, actually, I can't determine where exactly the unit is coming from, but this report is sent to the SSNO OB department and the 12th Corps OB department amongst other addressees and it's an information, and it says -- it's dated the 30th of September and it says as follows: "On 27th September 1991, four volunteers, who had set off to join the JNA units, allegedly returned ... from the territory of Dalj and Erdut." Now, let me first of all ask you this question: Is it possible to volunteer for a JNA unit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible given the -- I mean, the legal provisions that redefine volunteers as people who had no military obligations, because if they had military obligations they would have been most likely mobilised. There were also several mobilisations during that time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: "On the same day at the office of Stevan Malesevic, the president of the Ruma Municipal Assembly and in the presence of the secretary of the Ruma MSUP and his OB ... an interview was conducted with Knezevic and Jovanovic who left an impression of being a little inebriated." Over the page. "In the course of the interview, they stated that on 21 September, together with other volunteers and conscripts who had responded to the call-up, they had been transferred from the Ruma garrison to Dalj in the organisation of Major Vuckovac. Around 80 of them arrived and approximately half of them were left that night at around 2300 hours in the middle of the village until Vuckovac found a unit to turn them over to. Ten minutes later, Arkan, who in the opinion of interlocutors, is connected with the JNA superior officers and SUP officials, came along. " Now, just reading that, does that seem to relate to or could it relate to the September contingent of soldiers? Ruma, for your information, is in Serbia. I think it's about 40 kilometres south of Sremska Mitrovica. Is this referring to the same group?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, Your Honours, but I think it's unlikely in a sense there was -- there are the regular call-ups for people to join the JNA conscripts, but they wouldn't go directly to unit, they would first go through some kind of a recruitment or selection centre in order to look at -- to consider their physical and mental ability. Maybe some people are more fit for infantry and others are more fit for armour or for airborne or whatever, and so a selection would be made based also on the requirements of the various JNA units, and then obviously people would be given training before being assigned to a specific unit. Here we seem to see a situation where people are brought in by a person, a Major Vuckovac, and they move -- apparently they move directly to -- from Ruma to Dalj, which I would say is unusual. I know there was a lot of chaos at the time, limited response to call-ups or mobilisations, limited response to the -- I mean the conscript service. At the same time you have politically motivated volunteers or individuals who say whatever their status is, I want to go and defend the country. So, yeah, it's -- for me it's a different situation than the regular conscript contingents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Further down the page [Microphone not activated] --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Further down the page: "Through the hitherto checking, a statement was received from Major Vuckovac from Ruma," so that's the individual who escorted these individuals, these conscripts or volunteers, "from Ruma asserting that on 21.09," so that's the 21st of September, "he had handed over this group, which Knezevic and Jovanovic are talking about to the commander of the headquarters administration, Captain First Class Jovan Konjevic ..." Now, what is a headquarters administration and which headquarters administration would be in Dalj at this time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm looking at the B/C/S text. It is -- I mean, the only headquarters that is in Dalj at that moment is the headquarters of the 12th Novi Sad Corps, i.e., the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] So what's being described in this document is that someone from Ruma, either part of the JNA or the TO, accompanies a group of conscripts and/or volunteers, brings them to the headquarters administration of the 12th Corps in Dalj, leaves them there, and then apparently they're handed over to Arkan and Arkan takes them to the training centre and trains them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently, yeah. This is the -- I mean, what the report is stating.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Would that be indicative to you that Arkan is subordinated to the JNA at this time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On face value, it doesn't give any indication in relation to the -- any subordination or other relation Arkan and his group may have with the JNA. What it's -- indicates that there is at least co-operation between the 12th Corps and Arkan, whereby Arkan is used to train volunteers/conscripts that are to serve in the 12th Corps. So there is at least co-operation which also involves recognition by the 12th Corps of Arkan and his role in the training of volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Does the fact that Arkan attended the funeral of the first commander of OG North and for that matter the 12th Corps, General Bratic, in early October, does that provide any indication that he was acting as part and parcel of the JNA at this time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, from a military point of view not because attendance to funerals or ceremonies can mean anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Does the fact that General Panic said - and you're well familiar I think with the quotation - and actually I need to read the entire quotation because I suggest to you, Mr. Theunens, that you incorrectly interpret this passage as being only a reference to Arkan's participation in OG South or on attacks in Vukovar. And I'll -- and it's in your report at page 464, you locate it in a section on Vukovar, but let me read the passage for you and I suggest it's a little bit broader. In a question to General Panic, speaking in 1994 -- and for the record this is 04931, Prosecution tab 462. "Q. Was this chaos, was this chaos" -- and, yes, this is in relation to Vukovar that the questioner is asking. "The reason why so many -- there were not so many but these groups of um Serb volunteers, Serb volunteer forces, paramilitaries turned up on the scene in September. Was that the reason -- was that how it all happened?" Panic's answer was: "I think the operative units did their job correctly, but the mobilised did ... units were not prepared adequately for action, and when you don't prepare them adequately you have er ... you encounter the problems that you just mentioned. And that's how volunteers started appearing and we trained them for action er for combat action in Belgrade and they were fighting together with our units er ... they included Arkan's Tigers and er ... Seselj's Chetniks. They were not big groups, say in Arkan's case between 80 and 120 persons and in Seselj's case um between 90 and 120 men. But the people who wanted to act," and here's the key phrase, "all these formations were under command but the people who wanted to act independently were being removed from that area and disarmed and returned home." Now, do you agree with me that when you look at the entire context it certainly seems as if General Panic is talking more -- well, he's talking about the period starting in September; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He doesn't -- Panic doesn't give a specific time-frame, but it's -- as you mention -- because I'm a bit confused, you seem to suggest that I incorrectly described or identified something. I'm trying to figure out what you mean by that. Panic doesn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let me just clarify before you embark on an answer because I don't want to impute to you something that you haven't done, but at page 464 that quotation from Panic appears only in relation in a section about Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, this happens when you have amalgamated reports that parts are cut out of -- or cut and pasted of other reports. The Hadzic report I compiled in September /October 2012 when I had the new documents attempted also to cover operations in other parts of SBWS, but this -- the section which you are now discussing comes from the report on the Vukovar operations which, I mean, in my view it's quite obvious that I relate to Vukovar. And you yourself when quoting from this BBC interview given by Panic refer to the Vukovar area. So I don't see the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm past time, Mr. President. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Gosnell. Mr. Theunens, we take the second break and come back at 12.45. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps before the witness is brought in, I have some information with respect to the document which was MFI'd pending translation, this was Exhibit P1692. And if you remember, it was the item number 3 which Mr. Theunens was requesting a revision as to whether the word "officers" should be "superiors." We have received an answer from CLSS that they stand by their translation and that it should not be amended or changed in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So at this stage should we -- there's no further translations needed, can we exhibit it in full?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, just while the witness is taking his seat perhaps we could bring up 04 -- oh, I suppose that's ... Could we have 04931 which is Prosecution tab 462.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, I'm sorry for that last passage. I should have had it up on the screen and instead I just read it to you and that wasn't completely fair. So now I would like to have it on the screen in front of you, and the page is the page number ending 7848. I think this the B/C/S it's around 4968. Now, Mr. Theunens, so you're clear, I wasn't suggesting that you were attempting to slant your report in a particular way. It's just that the report that actually was submitted to the Judges, this quotation appears in that particular section on specifically Vukovar. But when you read this passage as a whole, would you agree that he does, you know, in his description of how it is that volunteers started appearing in the theatre, that he's describing a broader phenomenon here than merely which units are there on the front with Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honours. I mean, this is what General Panic states in the interview for BBC Death of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We would tender that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked -- Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We don't have any objections, but this document is part of the package that we would be offering. I think for the time being we could admit it but just as a marker. This is part of the documents that are footnoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Whichever way is most convenient for the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If I may assist, Your Honours, the record shows that the Defence does not object to the admission of this document which is on our list, so when the time comes for deliberation perhaps on the matter of our motion that could be taken into consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's keep it in the package then. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 1028 which is Defence tab 304. And if we could please go to page 72 of the English, and I believe it's around page 68 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, again, Mr. Theunens, this is a transcript of the -- of a session of the SFRY Presidency. Their Honours have seen this before and so I'm not going to read the entire passage, but I just want to put a very specific passage to you. And it's the part where Kostic is speaking down at the bottom of the page. And he says: "Zivota," and that's Zivota Panic, "at a session here once I asked what was the relationship between Arkan and the JNA and you were the one who told me that he was good." And then we get a response not from Panic but from someone else, Borisav Jovic, and the answer is or comment is: "In matters of war." And then Kostic says: "We should avoid any major clashes now, this should be done in a nice way so that these lads of his can stay, if they want, in the army." Panic's response: "Arkan carried out missions in the area very efficiently. At one point he broke away, but they brought him back, et cetera. However, he is doing Yugoslavia a disservice. He should be called and given a task. Those who sent him there should call him. I do not know who sent him. However, Arkan was present in Bijeljina, Zvornik, around Sarajevo, Knin, et cetera. Someone is leading him and issuing tasks to him. We should see who is doing this. It is certain that it is not us." And then he -- at the end of his passage he says: "Since I have to attend talks with Vance at 1700 hours, could I leave, please?" Do you believe what Zivota Panic is saying here, that he doesn't know who has sent Arkan or who is sending him?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I just ask a question. Can you remind me what the time of this meeting is, I mean the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Certainly. This is the 194th Session of the Presidency -- yeah, and that occurred on the 16th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992, yeah. From a contextual point of view, this is after the SFRY presidential order of the 10th of December, 1991, so the presidential order number 73 on the engagement of volunteers during an imminent state of war -- or imminent threat of war, I'm sorry. I mean, one of the points in that order is that all volunteers should be subordinated to the JNA within the ten days -- all volunteer formations, actually, and that's an important clarification, or they shall be removed. My understanding of the context is and given the date of this meeting is that Panic is referring to the appearance of Arkan and his volunteers during operations in northern Bosnia-Herzegovina like Bijeljina and Zvornik and these operations, as I have addressed in other reports for other trials, were focused at implementing some of the six strategic goals, in this particular context establishing a corridor between Semberija and Krajina. And -- I mean Panic -- I think he's -- he asks a number of questions because he knows that -- and again this is corroborated by JNA documents concerning these -- the events in Bijeljina, Zvornik, and so on during that time-period. It's not the -- Arkan is not operating under JNA command or is there and has not been -- I mean not systematically and has apparently, based on what Panic says, not been sent by the JNA, so the question is, well, who is doing it then. And I think the fact that Panic raised these questions during a meeting of the SFRY Presidency suggests that Arkan -- that Panic expects that his interlocutors there may be in a better position to provide him with an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So the answer to my question was yes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it -- I mean, it is reasonable to assume that Panic was in a position to make an assessment or to draw certain conclusions as to who had sent Arkan because there were also security organs discussing -- I mean reports discussing this matter, i.e., the relations between Arkan and the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia. But probably - and I don't know the context, further context that is discussed in this meeting - probably he wants the members of the SFRY Presidency to formally state to him who is giving these assignments to Arkan. Given indications Panic has -- this is a continuation of the sentence, given the indications Panic has concerning relations Arkan enjoys with the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If this is part of the package, I'll just say for the record we don't have an objection, or if it's not part of the package we would tender that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document was admitted yesterday through Witness Nielsen, though yet without an exhibit number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So just to put a point on General Panic's attitude as you can discern it in this transcript. It seems that what you're saying is that he's being slightly disingenuous, that he has information but he's not sure. Is that a fair summary of your answer?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think -- I wouldn't use the expression disingenuous. I don't know what Panic's state of mind was at the time. But it is -- I mean JNA reports talk about presence of Arkan. The documents -- the JNA documents I have seen don't clarify or don't indicate how Arkan is appearing in which circumstances he's appearing in Bijeljina, Zvornik, and other locations in Bosnia-Herzegovina spring 1992, and Arkan and his people are conducting certain activities there. In the absence of JNA documents concerning -- I mean orders to Arkan to do these activities or to be there, the question can be raised: Well, who is it then that has given these assignments to Arkan. That is one element. The second element is that already from security organ reports from the 1st Military District covering the October 1991 to, say, January 1992 time-period, the security organs gather information indicating the existence of special or specific relations between Arkan and officials of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia. So I think it would be logical even for Panic to assume that if he hasn't ordered Arkan to be in Bijeljina and Zvornik, then it should have been or then it would have been the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia -- of other members of the Government of Serbia. But he -- now he wants to, at least according to these minutes, he wants to check with the remaining members of the SFRY Presidency whether they can explain to him why and how it comes that Arkan is involved and is conducting military activities in these locations, Bijeljina, Zvornik, and others. Because maybe it has been approved by the SFRY Presidency. I haven't seen any such documents, but these are all assumptions Panic can make and my understanding from his questions during the minutes is that he seeks clarification from -- well, actually, the Supreme Command, i.e., the highest command organ in existence in SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: One thing is clear, he's denying that he's the one who sent Arkan; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because otherwise the question would seem rather unusual, and then I think when you look at the rest of the minutes they would have answered to him: Well, you know, Zivota, you sent him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P101, Prosecution tab 244.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is a document that you refer to in your report on several occasions, so you're well familiar with it. And it's one of these security organ reports you have been referring to addressing the issue of Arkan.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's another document we have. I mean at least here on the screen we have something from the SAO SBWS.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It should be 65 ter 00873.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P1004. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, I called for P101.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: What I meant is that 65 ter document 873 is admitted as the Prosecution Exhibit P1004. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's clearly my handwriting failing me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is from some time in January, and if we could please go to page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And, sorry, just for the record that's written by chief Colonel Milic Jovanovic. Or it's for Milic Jovanovic. If we could have page 4 of the English. We seem to be on page 6 of the English. Well, let's see if we can go back in the English and see if we get to the right passage. And back one more page, please. There appears to be a page missing or out of order. Well, could we just go down to the bottom of that page, please. There it is. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, here we see midway through the paragraph that says "it is known." It says: [As read] "Our assessment is that certain" possibly "JNA leaders accept him on the - illegible - and influence of these circles. It is a telling fact that although Raznatovic has small forces at his disposal, he attends meetings of the 1st Military District command with the corps commanders ..." Who is the commander of the 1st Military District for most of this time-period up between August and up until the date of this document which is January 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is general -- Colonel-General Zivota Panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So the same individual who in the previous document is claiming he doesn't know who is sending Arkan to the area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I think we're talking about two different issues. In the previous document General Panic was inquiring about the involvement of Arkan in northern Bosnia-Herzegovina, at least two or three months after this document. So the situation is -- I mean, I'm not here to defend Panic whatsoever, but it -- I mean, from a methodological point of view, drawing analytical conclusions is something else than just comparing two different documents and saying then saying it must be this. So the situation is different. It is clear again in the context of the JNA and the events in Vukovar that Arkan enjoys good relations with the 12th Corps and in particular with General Andrija Biorcevic who becomes commander of the 12th Corps I think at the latest early November or maybe in the course of November 1991 already, I mean after the previous commander, General Bratic, is killed in action. And I've mentioned that a few times, but that is the most telling example, the famous video of a reception where Biorcevic is praising Arkan clearly shows that there are good -- not just on a personal level but also on a professional level good relations between General Biorcevic on the one hand and Arkan on the other hand. So referring to this meeting, it may well be that Biorcevic has brought Arkan with him to that meeting or several meetings, I mean meetings of the 1st Military District, or maybe that Panic invited him, I don't know, but there are different explanations possible and so again I'm alone, but what I tried to clarify is there is not necessarily a contradiction between what Panic says at a meeting of the SFRY Presidency in relation to events three months later and what is stated in this security organs report of the 2nd of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: As a military man what does it tell you that an individual with, say, 100, 150 troops under his command is attending a meeting with corps commanders?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could say size doesn't matter, but I don't want to, I mean, try to be witty. It shows that Arkan and his group is considered an important component, and this is also reflected through other documents. Whether that is because of the value, the combat value, of his forces or the relations Arkan has with, as I mentioned, Biorcevic - and this is also indicated in other documents, security organ's reports, I mean the relations Arkan enjoys or allegedly enjoys with members of the Serbian government, in particular MUP and MOD - that I cannot establish. Maybe both played a role.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: From a military perspective, don't you view it remarkable that a man with a company-strength unit appears to be attending meetings of corps commanders at the district level?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we could try to give some military flavour to it in stating that maybe the 12th Corps was using Arkan and his group during combat operations as a kind of strategic reserve, which would actually be quite consistent with General Biorcevic's assessment of the role and of the role of Arkan's volunteers during operations. And that assessment I refer to the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 00356, please, Prosecution tab 93, P103.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we've looked at this document earlier today. Now I'd like you to look at a different part of it and it's on page 2 of the English. [As read] "While staying in the forward command post of the 12th Corps, agricultural estate in Dalj on 29 and 30 September, the source saw Arkan armed and coming to the area of the IKM in the off-road vehicle two times and entering the building where the command was located." So you'd agree here we see an indication he's also visiting the command of the -- the forward command post of the 12th Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and that's consistent with what I said concerning his relations -- I mean, Biorcevic is at that time not yet commander of the 12th Corps, but relations between Arkan and the 12th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that command post is at the agricultural estate in Dalj; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as is stated in the document, the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, if we could go back again to 873 to the same area where we were in the document before, which I think is page 2. And, sir, you rely on this -- as I said before, this particular document and this passage. If I could just pose my question. It says there at the bottom of the page in this report: [As read] "It is known that it," so the centre, even though the document doesn't expressly say which centre, but it says "the centre is financed in ways that are not fully known. It is known that it is financed by the socialist party of Serbia from within the country and from abroad as well as by numerous enterprises. Accordingly, a characteristic example is the Dalj farm which," and then it says illegible question mark, "written order of Goran Hadzic was paid out 7.088.674 dinars and 50 cents for the needs of the illegible guard while illegible for free." Now, you've recited that information in your report. Do you consider that claim reliable?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do for several reasons. In the Milosevic trial we had a financial analyst preparing a report on financial aspects of role of Mr. Milosevic in relation to certain events. And I remember seeing documents, I mean payment orders from several agricultural enterprises or state-owned enterprises in SBWS signed by members of the SAO SBWS government for payments or the transfer of goods to the Erdut training centre at different moments in time, including even if I recall well end of 1991 as well as 1992 and subsequent. So what I'm trying to say is that I've seen other documents including copies of payment order that corroborate this passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 05135, please, which is Prosecution tab 538.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And just while that's coming up, if I can just ask you to go back a little bit and that was yesterday or perhaps it was earlier today, you suggested that there might be a contradiction in the documents to the extent that on the one hand we see JNA documents showing that Arkan has a close relationship with various people and then on the other hand we see various OB reports in which his activities are being reported upon. Now, I wonder if you could accept that contradiction is one interpretation, but isn't it also true that if he's subordinated to the JNA that actually it's precisely the obligation of the OB organs to ascertain whether he is engaging in criminal activity, and then if there is credible evidence about that to pass it on for prosecution to the military prosecutors?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, and maybe I misexpressed myself yesterday or the previous days. I didn't want to suggest that the documents are contradictory.
