I do believe when looking at all the documents that different elements of the JNA enjoy different relations with Mr. Arkan, summarising in two lines, okay, General Panic reportedly orders to subordinate all elements that are on the battle-field to the JNA, that also implies Arkan but there are problems with that so there are several orders for that. The 12th Corps enjoying quite close relations with Arkan, including also their use during combat operations under the order of the 12th Corps. And then indeed at the same time security organs of the 1st Military District writing reports on the activities of Arkan. The fact that they write reports on the activities of Arkan and his group does not necessarily mean that Arkan is subordinated to the JNA or not. I mean, wasn't doesn't imply the other, one doesn't exclude the other. So coming back to the question then -- but of course if Arkan and his group are committing crimes or other activities that are prohibited by SFRY armed forces doctrine, then it's up to the security organs to report about that and we would expect the implementation of the military discipline or mainly the military justice system. And on --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So just to put a fine point on it --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- and I apologise for interrupting, the existence of these reports is perfectly consistent with his subordination; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I said that one does not imply the other. The existence of these reports --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, that wasn't my question. My question was: Is it consistent?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't understand the question. What do you mean it is consistent? What does -- why -- what do you mean by the use of the word "consistent," given my answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The question is whether or not the existence of those reports is consistent with his subordination to the JNA? That's all.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I mean, I've answered the question. In my view it is as I explained, the reports where the security organs on a group do not suggest whether or not this group is subordinated to the JNA. Of course, if the report states that he is subordinated to the JNA, that would be a useful element of information in order to establish his relations with the JNA, but at face value a security organ report as such without -- and that doesn't mention whether or not he's subordinated to the JNA, doesn't give us any useful information as to whether or not he's subordinated to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, Mr. Theunens asked you what you mean by "is consistent with." It could be a language problem. And when you answer that question, in fact you didn't answer, you just repeated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You're right, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that, Mr. Theunens. It could be we're just using two different concepts of the word. And let me put it a slightly different way. It does not negate that there was a subordination relationship, the existence of these OB documents? It does not disprove that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've answered the question. You know, it doesn't negate it, it doesn't confirm it, unless there are elements that allow to draw conclusions in relation to his subordination relationship with the JNA in the security organs reports and then it would be useful elements of information that would require other elements of information, situation reports or orders, in order to confirm the nature of the relation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Assuming that there is a subordination relationship with the unit, is it understood as a matter of JNA practice, doctrine, or any rules that are in existence that logistical support needs to be provided to that subordinated unit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to give a general answer or to focus the answer on Arkan?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It could be hazardous but I'll ask you to first start generally and then perhaps we can go to Arkan.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the general answer is yes, and this is also reiterated in different, I mean, documents of the 1st Military District. We have discussed these and they are in my report that the JNA was responsible for providing supply, I mean logistics supply, to all subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. And now let's move on to Arkan.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For Arkan the matter is slightly more complicated because we know - and I think that's also addressed in security organ's reports - that Arkan, for example, has more sophisticated weapons, I'm not talking about heavy weapons, but like, for example, more sophisticated infantry weapons, even of Western origin, that are not available in the inventory of the SFRY armed forces. So where it would be impossible for the JNA to provide specific logistics support for those weapons, is it ammunition or for their maintenance. For other parts, yes, the JNA would be required, I mean if Arkan is operating under their command, to provide logistics support for the items they are in the position to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. So now let's take a look at the document in front of us. And it's written by Arkan. Apparently it is addressed to the Dalj socially owned enterprise and the director thereof. And it says: "During a review of expenses specified as the expenditures of the Territorial Defence Special Training Centre, we found out that according to your breakdown the total expenses for December were as follows ..." And then there's a listing of payments or -- I would say invoices, they've been charged a certain amount of money and this is -- and he is setting that out. And then he says: "Two factors participated in spending the amount of 3.4 "and some odd million "dinars. The government and its ministries and the special training centre of the Territorial Defence of the SO SBWS. We maintain that the expenses of these two factors must be separated, which is what we did for December 1991. We thus come to the conclusion that the expenses in the amount mentioned above could be broken down as follows ... "We therefore kindly request from you that in the future our expenses be specified separately, whereby we will be able to determine our expenses more easily." Isn't this, in fact, a letter of complaint from Arkan to the Dalj farm saying: Stop overcharging us?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, this is one of the elements of information you can find in the letter. There are also other ones. I mean, it's remarkable in my view given the focus of my report that Arkan - and I forgot the date but I think it's January 1992 if we can go to the top again --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It is January 1992.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That Arkan then signs as apparently the commander of the special -- sorry, if you can go back to the heading, as a commander or as in having an official capacity in relation to the special training centre of the TO of the SAO SBWS. I find it remarkable given the various allegations that have been made in 1st Military District reports but, I mean, there is also information in open sources at that time about his role in combat and his alleged involvement in crimes. He and his group -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, we're certainly going to come to that issue, but now let's focus on the point which I'm trying to raise with you which I don't think you answered. Do you agree with me that this is a letter of complaint about being overbilled?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, he complains that he's -- I mean, that expenses by other official organs of the SAO SBWS are charged to him or to the training centre where in his view they should be charged to these other official bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, looking back or thinking back to P101, you remember that's the security organ report which you rely on in your report repeatedly for the claim that Goran Hadzic has ordered the Dalj farm to support Arkan. Does it make any sense that on the one hand there's going to be an order for the Dalj farm to support Arkan or subsidize Arkan and then in January Arkan is complaining about being overcharged by that very same institution?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe it's an issue of accounting and that is outside my area of expertise that in order to ensure that their accounts are clear they check with Arkan: Okay, these and these expenses have been made for you, and that would be consistent with the claim in the security organ's report, and, yeah, they want to have this clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you're saying that they're receiving some kind of a -- you're hypothesising that they're receiving a credit of some sort from the Dalj farm, then they've somehow been overcharged, and then now they have to write this letter complaining about it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, and also I think now we are talking about the situation that Arkan is in charge of the Territorial Defence special training centre. I'm not sure whether in the security organ's report we're already talking about the Territorial Defence training centre or just Arkan's training centre in Erdut. Yeah, I mean -- I don't have the two documents in front of me, but I would say that okay if the Dalj farm or socially owned enterprise has to provide or provides financial -- I mean provides support, supplies or whatever, to Arkan, they need to put that somewhere in their books, the numbers and so on. And the next question would of course be: Who would pay? Would Arkan pay or is somebody else? Now, if Arkan is paying, where does he get the money from in order to pay these bills because the Territorial Defence training centre doesn't produce any use any economical revenue, so the payment Arkan has to provide according to these documents to the Dalj socially owned enterprise has to come from somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It probably isn't coming from the very socially owned enterprise that is overcharging him though. Wouldn't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I haven't analysed how the SAO SBWS was organising its budget and ensuring if, for example, Arkan received certain services or supplies, how those -- that provided those services were reimbursed and how Arkan whether he got his money from. The money has to come from somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It was already admitted and marked as P215.140. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, after that rather long and perhaps taxing journey through documents about Arkan 's direct connections with very senior levels of the JNA, Arkan's direct operations in conjunction with JNA forces, I say starting at the beginning of August and continuing for months, considering what Panic says both when he's being a little more honest and when he's being a little bit less honest, given what we see in the report about the engagement in Dalj and Trajkovic's lack of honesty, I suggest to you, and given all the other information about how Arkan is interacting with JNA forces, in the area of responsibility of the 12th Corps, are you willing to agree with me that Arkan is subordinated to the 12th Corps, let's start with throughout the period of 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have answered the question. I'm not going to -- I don't see a reason to change my answer. I could just clarify -- I mean, Mr. Gosnell is suggesting that senior officers of the JNA are lacking honesty. Again, I cannot express a view on that. I can only refer to doctrine, that is, that it was a violation of military discipline and maybe even more serious for an officer to provide inaccurate reporting. And given the system or procedure that a commander has to be familiar with the activities or the situation of his units two levels down, there were ways to find out if somebody was providing inaccurate reporting, especially in a context of such a serious issue like the presence of Arkan and his volunteers and their activities in SBWS during fall 1991. I -- for sure I don't dispute that Arkan was subordinated to the JNA, i.e., to units of the 12th Corps at particular moments in time, but there are also activities conducted by Arkan where his relation with the JNA is not entirely clear, even if - and I fully agree - according to doctrine and according to Panic's orders, 15th of October, 16th of November, the JNA was -- should have subordinated all units or remove them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And when you refer to activities, I assume you're referring to criminal activities; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, Your Honours, yeah. I mean, the Dalj prison events is one example.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The fact that a subordinate soldier is or let me not use the word "subordinate." The fact that a soldier is committing a crime in violation of all the laws of war and the regulations of the army, that's surely not indicative that the person isn't subordinated; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, then let me put it a different way. If an artillery commander takes direct aim at a town and blows it to pieces, surely it's no argument to say the person isn't subordinated because they violated the laws of war; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if someone purporting to enforce security in a zone of responsibility unlawfully walks around, loots houses, beats people, kills them, that's no indication that the person isn't subordinated, is it, to the unit in the area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not, but do you want me to refer to -- I mean, is this referring to Arkan or are these just general questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, shouldn't the answers to both be the same?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly when seen in context of who Arkan was and what he was doing and the various security organs' reports or other reports. I mean, there's -- I haven't addressed those in my report, but there were so many reports in the media about him kind of glorifying his activities, the activities of him and his group, he's not the ordinary soldier or the ordinary artillery commander. From the reports I've reviewed, I'm repeating myself, I'm sorry for that, but it is reasonable to conclude that Arkan enjoys particular relations with senior officials in Serbia and also in the SAO SBWS. And maybe the existence of these relations prevented or, I don't know, discouraged certain JNA officers to really enforce military discipline and military justice as they should have done. I discussed I think also with Mr. Demirdjian. We have these security organ reports. Unfortunately, we don't have the follow-up. What did the competent authorities, military prosecutor, others, or the civilian prosecutor in Serbia, do with these reports? Did they act upon them? I'm not aware that Arkan or any members of his group were ever arrested in Serbia, at least not between 1991 and 1993. Arkan was even allowed to establish a political party and he participated in the political -- in the elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- thank you. I'm going to move on now.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I think earlier - and you should correct me if I'm wrong in making this statement - but earlier we established that a president of a republic, whether in peace or war time, has no command authority over the TO in that republic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: After 1988 that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And in the area of the 12th Corps, what does have that command responsibility over the TO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the commander. Sorry, the commander of the 12th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Does that mean that when we see references to the -- to individual TO units, it's the 12th Corps that has command authority over those various TO institutions?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with, again, two clarifications, that is, according to doctrine they should have and when we're talking about TO I'm talking about the TO -- I mean, the republican TO and the TO of the two autonomous provinces, Kosovo and Vojvodina, as it was defined in SFRY armed forces doctrine. The situation becomes much more complex when we are talking about the self-established SAO SBWS or SAO Krajina or SAO Western Slavonia. I call them local Serb, but TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The Erdut training centre as a matter of let's start with doctrine, given the circumstances, that is supposed to be subordinated to the 12th Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think maybe you can refresh my memory, when it is -- when the Erdut training centre starts to be officially called a SAO -- I mean, SO Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem training centre -- sorry, SAO SBWS TO training centre. And then -- because indeed that's also complexity because then we have to look at what are the relations between the SAO SBWS TO and the 12th Corps? As long as the 12th Corps is in the area, then I would agree with you. I mean is present in SBWS, then I would agree with you. A lot of time the situation is more complex especially also, just coming back to the beginning of my answer, when the Erdut training centre is only used by Arkan, I think, for training and when his group is there and when at least based on my review of the documents the link or the relation with the SAO SBWS TO is not entirely clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a JNA document that refers to the SAO SBWS TO dated 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that uses the three words in that connection, SAO SBWS TO?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That refers to an overarching TO that unites the subordinate or individual town TOs, have you ever seen such a document that refers to that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly. I mean, I think -- what I mentioned in examination this is for the SAO SBWS civilian authorities, there it's for the first time actually on the 20th of November in his order I think it was 2436-1 that General Panic explicitly recognises these authorities. I mention this because this is the only context that I remember that SAO SBWS is used in an official document and as a recognised entity by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You can't tell from looking at that header whether or not the training centre has been set up by the district government, can you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. I mean, if I would make abstraction of the context then I would say, you know, since according to the legislation in the SFRY, the republics are responsible for training the TO, then I would say well it has to be the republic but then the question arises, well, it's for sure not the Republic of Croatia. Then we end up in the context, so you could say from a purely theoretical point of view it has to be the SAO SBWS or the RSK. But as I highlighted, the situation is quite complex so it may well be that the centre was established by the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't -- sorry, I haven't seen a document that is establishing the centre and for sure I haven't seen a JNA document to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, here's the fallacy in your reasoning, Mr. Theunens, and I do understand why I believe you're engaging in this fallacy. Why can't it be that just as there are neighbourhoods in Vukovar like the Leva Supoderica neighbourhood where there is a TO, just as there is a town called Dalj where there is a TO set up by local people, just as there is a Bapska TO that is basically a formation that comes out of village guards, various other TOs, why is it necessary or why should you assume, because I think that's what you're doing, that there is an overarching provincial or district TO headquarters General Staff that somehow is organising all of those individual TOs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You make several suggestions in your question. I mean, my reference to the existence of a SAO SBWS TO -- well, you know, in the heading of the document in front of us, it is mentioned special training centre of the Territorial Defence of the SO - sorry, I touched the screen - SO Baranja, Western Srem in Erdut. I didn't invent that. It's on the document. It's a contemporaneous document. The certificate we discussed this morning signed by Radovan Stojicic talks about the Supreme Command or the supreme headquarters of the TO of SAO of the SBWS. Those I would say that's the situation how it is in practice. And what I was explaining earlier with the legislation is de jure aspect. Of course, everyone can establish his own unit, but then it's a matter of, I would say, recognition because otherwise you get chaos. And we see --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And who does the recognising?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is -- that is in -- a complex matter in the context of the situation in SAO Krajina or SBWS in fall 1991 because as you remember the document we discussed during examination where the Chief of Staff Trajkovic of the 12th Corps asks the commander of the 1st Military District: Well, what is the attitude we should adopt towards these SAO authorities and the -- maybe he didn't use "local Serb TO" but local TO and the 1st Military District? Well, until the 20th of November states that no interference should be allowed by these "self-declared" or local organs of authority. And this is, for example -- this is discussed on pages 491 to 496 of my report. And I agree with you, at the same time you see that the 12th Corps enjoys close or uses Arkan and so on during its operations so --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- you raise a very interesting point. Here we have a document which you're referring to from the 15th of October, 1991, where General Panic is saying: Don't pay any attention yet to this -- these SBWS civilian structures at the same time, as we know well having looked at the documents, that he has sent Arkan, he has been involved in Arkan's presence in the area of the 12th Corps and obviously is operating with him and involved with him. Now, that being the case, who do you think is providing the authority to put that letter-head right there in that document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, again, these are for me totally different matters because as I mentioned earlier I haven't seen any JNA document -- I mean, maybe you can show me one, but I don't recall seeing any JNA document whereby the JNA establishes training centres for the TO. When we go back to the de jure situation, the republics and the autonomous provinces, i.e., Kosovo and Vojvodina, when they had that status, are responsible for the training and equipping and organisation of the TO, so it would be their responsibility. And again, when we look at the situation as it develops in fall 1991, the JNA may have provided assistance but then again I would like to see specific documents, but I cannot draw from any conclusions based on your suggestion that given the fact that Arkan at times operates under the command of the 12th Corps in command operations, that therefore the 1st Military District must have been responsible for establishing the training centre. I cannot draw that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you'd like to see specific documents indicating that, but as you said there are a lot of OG North documents that appear to be missing or have never been provided?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe -- yeah, maybe there are some documents included there, but we have a fairly detailed -- I mean, we have a quite substantial -- or "we," the Office of the Prosecutor had a quite substantial collection of documents concerning the operations of OG South and also, for example, for other parts of Croatia, the Krajina, where indeed the JNA provides support to the local Serb TO, and I'm talking now about fall 1991, I'm not talking about the situation after January 1992 where, indeed, as we have seen, the JNA, I mean the SSNO, provides substantial support to organising local Serb TO units. But prior to that -- I mean including their training. But prior to that, I haven't seen a document for the establishment of a training centre, so -- and it has not been reported by any of the documents of the 1st Military District I have seen concerning the training centre Arkan is -- I mean is in charge of in Erdut in January 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Prior to starting your testimony here, did you review the transcripts of Mr. Nielsen's -- Dr. Nielsen's testimony?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, Your Honours. From time to time when I look at the Sense Tribunal web site and there was a -- I think they paraphrased Mr. Nielsen's testimony, but I find it difficult to understand because also I review what they write in other cases of my testimony and I'm sometimes also surprised. I have the impression that they're not always fully versed with the details or the specific aspects of military doctrine or in the case of Dr. Nielsen, MUP, I mean Ministry of Interior activities and police doctrine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Have you heard the thesis expressed that the training centre in Erdut was controlled by one or another organ from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, from my work at the Belgium Ministry of Defence, I started to look at the Balkans in September 1992. I went for the first time to Erdut in August 1993. At various times obviously and since Belgian troops were deployed in Baranja since I think April or May 1992 until the course of 1997, the presence of Arkan and his activities was of relevance for us, not to the least for force protection issues. And various information concerning Arkan's relations with Belgrade as well as with Mr. Hadzic were available, but obviously I haven't used them for my report. For my report I rely on JNA and other official documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Why are you mentioning it here if it's not part of your report? What relevance is that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I tried to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you take that into account in preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took it into account -- I mean, I haven't explained the methodology, so if you want I can explain the methodology. But interpretation of the information is a step in the processing phase of the intelligence cycle. Interpretation means that you compare new information that you have obtained or information you were not aware of before with the existing "body" of knowledge and then you draw certain conclusions. So in this particular context, imagine that I assumed or that I was convinced that Arkan -- say that Arkan was sent by President Milosevic, assuming that. Well, before I would put that on paper, I would look for information in order to establish or to see whether I would be in a position to establish who sent Arkan on the basis of the information in front of me. Since I didn't see any such JNA documents except for the security organ reports who do not answer that question I think very clearly, but they make suggestions as to the nature of relations Arkan enjoys with officials in Belgrade, so I was not able to answer that question so I haven't made any statement in the report or statement by me that Arkan was sent by President Milosevic, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But your report does frequently mention his connections with the Serbian MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, and as you will see from the footnotes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if I can just pose the next question. Isn't it also true that Badza, Radovan Stojicic, is also in your view and in your report closely associated with the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you use -- sorry. You say "in your view," well, that is my conclusion based on the documents I have reviewed, and I think I do it in a very transparent manner because these documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if -- I'm just --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. I mean, this is the second time you interrupt me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I'm in the President's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Theunens, you should consider from time to time to answer just with a yes or a no when it is possible and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, what I want --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if I can just ask -- just let me pose a few questions and then I promise, Mr. Theunens, if you then want to elaborate or give further answers, I'll be more than happy to allow you or to give a general question so you can do that. But if I can just ask you a few specific questions and then we'll get to the broader -- the broader answer. And my question is: Radovan Stojicic was, in your information, a fairly senior member of the Serbian MUP in 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And did you have any information that he controlled the border guards connecting the area of the SBWS with Serbia? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no specific recollection. Probably I saw something to that effect, but I haven't -- I don't believe I have mentioned that in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if Radovan Stojicic and Arkan show up at around the same time in the area of the SBWS, do you really think that they didn't on their own authority have the power to create a stamp referring to the TO of the SBWS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, anyone can create a stamp, but the question is: Why would you do it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, for the simple reason that there was a situation of chaos, confusion, and war. And in a time of war, the authorities that are powerful and who have the means will arrive and create institutions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it's a possibility, yeah. It can happen anywhere. I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this is all going on during a time of armed conflict; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In an area of operations by SFRY armed forces?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but then the problem arises -- I mean I understand now that you want to ask a specific question. I don't know how many footnotes there are in the -- I'm sorry to elaborate, but I don't know how many footnotes there are in the -- in the amalgamated report or let alone in the non-accepted report. But the volume of footnotes reflecting the volume of material I reviewed, and that material consists of official documents, one of the conclusions I drew in the report when I talk about OGs and TGs shows that there is a functioning system of command and control and a functioning system of reporting, so even if there is some chaos in relation, for example, to groups moving in and moving out, given the doctrine it's the task then -- I mean the JNA has to intervene and raise the issue and this is done by Panic and others. So there is no permanent chaos and I don't think -- I mean coming back to your question, if they fabricate the stamp themselves and maybe they established the training centre themselves, it needs to be equipped, people need to be fed there, people need to -- they need ammunition and so on, and this is something where sooner or later given also the location in Erdut and the isolation of Eastern Slavonia at that time that the supplies they need can only come from Serbia. And I don't think you could just cross one of the bridges with a truck with ammunition or rifles or whatever equipment that was used in the training centre and everybody would close his or her eyes so that of course the authorities were aware of that. So I think I would moderate or qualify the use of the term "chaos" in its correct proportions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the institution that's imposing order in this situation and that has a mechanism of reporting and command is the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. And the difficulties they face are also reflected in the various orders they issue where they actually repeat the same order to enforce control over the area throughout fall 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Perhaps just one document before we finish, 00658. Prosecution tab 188. This is from Mrksic dated the 21st of November, 1991, and I'm interested in the language being used in this document and the addressees.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, the first thing is there is no reference at all to any overarching TO staff of the autonomous district; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct and if you allow me I can provide my explanation for that or potential explanations for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let's go through a few more subordinate questions and then if you want to provide an answer, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But we do see that the addressees include apparently the commander of Seselj's forces volunteer detachment. There's a JNA unit listed there. There appears to be a TO Serbia unit listed there from Kragujevac. And then there is another JNA commander. Then there is the TO Vukovar commander and I don't know what the last -- who the last two addressees are. And it concerns the Leva Supoderica volunteers. Now, if the Leva Supoderica volunteers are in any way within a provincial staff or a provincial TO organisation with any strength or reality, wouldn't that staff have been addressed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've -- I mean, as I've explained, I haven't seen any documents from OG South referring to an SAO SBWS TO or a TO -- an SAO SBWS TO staff. So of course it's -- if such a staff existed, it should have been referred to in this document. Now, the issue here is what -- I mean whether OG South command recognised, even if an SAO SBWS TO staff may have existed - and I'm not answering that now, I'm not trying to answer that now - OG South obviously did not recognise these structures. And we have -- I'm not sure whether in the amalgamated report, but we have security organs reports also for OG South providing information on alleged interference and so on. And I agree with you that mentioning of the volunteer unit Seseljevci in a JNA document is unusual and, as I mentioned in the examination, it demonstrates the perception OG South command, i.e., the Guards Motorised Brigade command had over -- no, sorry, of, perception of the relations between these volunteers and Mr. Seselj and his party.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I see we're over time again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Mr. Gosnell. Mr. Theunens, the end of today's hearing. We'll see you again on Monday morning, 9.00. I wish you a good weekend.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 13th day of May, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 25
